title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
浙江鄉試小錄序
人君求賢以事天必養之於豫
而登之以賢科者欲其盡天
降之才與共天位食天祿而
治天民也肆
聖天子建極敷化純心圖治益謹
庠序之敎翕受俊造之升廼
===
成化庚子
詔天下開科取士聿循
舊章而申嚴之意有加浙江藩
憲重臣率先祗奉禮聘儒紳
來典文衡克謙幸與焉巡按
監察御史謝秉中綜理其事
暨提學副使胡榮合十一郡
punctuated:
浙江鄉試小錄序

人君求賢以事天，必養之於豫，而登之以賢科者，欲其盡天降之才，與共天位、食天祿，而治天民也。肆聖天子建極敷化，純心圖治，益謹庠序之敎，翕受俊造之升。廼成化庚子，詔天下開科取士，聿循舊章，而申嚴之意有加。浙江藩憲重臣率先祗奉，禮聘儒紳來典文衡，克謙幸與焉。巡按監察御史謝秉中綜理其事，暨提學副使胡榮合十一郡
translation_en:
Preface to the Brief Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination

When a ruler seeks worthy men with whom to serve Heaven, he must first nurture them in advance. In raising them to office through examinations for the worthy, he intends that they fully employ their Heaven-bestowed talents, share with him the positions conferred by Heaven, receive Heaven’s emoluments, and govern Heaven’s people. Thus our sagely Son of Heaven establishes the supreme standard and spreads moral transformation. With an undivided heart intent upon good government, he takes ever greater care over instruction in the schools and welcomes the advancement of men of outstanding talent and accomplishment.

Then, in the gengzi year of Chenghua [1480], an edict commanded the opening of examinations throughout the realm to select men for office. Established regulations were followed, with still greater emphasis on their strict enforcement. The senior officials of Zhejiang’s Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions took the lead in respectfully carrying out the command. With due ceremony they invited learned gentlemen to preside over the assessment of literary merit. I, Keqian, was fortunate to be among them. Xie Bingzhong, Investigating Censor serving as Regional Inspector, supervised the undertaking as a whole. Together with Hu Rong, Vice Commissioner for Education, he assembled those from the eleven prefectures …

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
士三千餘人一再試之擇其
經義論策頗通者千七百有
竒入場時則
欽差司設監太監張慶鎮守其地
巡鹽監察御史戴仁工部主
事郭秩皆在公所相與勸勉
賛襄冀成厥美内之提調監
===
試有左布政使劉璋按察使
楊繼宗左叅政左賛副使張
文外之綱維糾察有右叅政
吳森韓斐副使林傑左叅議
和遜右叅議張敷華梁鏞僉
事萬禮吳璵魏富潘珪錢山
張玉江孟綸李鑑爰及百執
punctuated:
士三千餘人，一再試之，擇其經義論策頗通者千七百有竒入場。時則欽差司設監太監張慶鎮守其地，巡鹽監察御史戴仁、工部主事郭秩皆在公所，相與勸勉賛襄，冀成厥美。
内之提調監試，有左布政使劉璋、按察使楊繼宗、左叅政左賛、副使張文；外之綱維糾察，有右叅政吳森、韓斐，副使林傑，左叅議和遜，右叅議張敷華、梁鏞，僉事萬禮、吳璵、魏富、潘珪、錢山、張玉、江孟綸、李鑑，爰及百執
translation_en:
…more than three thousand candidates were tested in successive rounds. Of these, more than seventeen hundred whose interpretations of the Classics, discourses, and policy essays showed considerable understanding were selected to enter the examination compound. At that time, Zhang Qing, Grand Eunuch of the Directorate of Imperial Accouterments, was stationed in the region by imperial commission. Dai Ren, Investigating Censor for Salt Inspection, and Guo Zhi, Bureau Secretary in the Ministry of Works, were also at the government offices. Together they offered encouragement and assistance, hoping to bring the undertaking to a successful conclusion.
Within the compound, those responsible for managing and supervising the examination were Liu Zhang, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner; Yang Jizong, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner; Zuo Zan, Left Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner; and Zhang Wen, Provincial Surveillance Vice Commissioner. Outside, responsibility for maintaining order and investigating irregularities fell to Wu Sen and Han Fei, Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioners; Lin Jie, Provincial Surveillance Vice Commissioner; He Xun, Left Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioner; Zhang Fuhua and Liang Yong, Right Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioners; and Wan Li, Wu Yu, Wei Fu, Pan Gui, Qian Shan, Zhang Yu, Jiang Menglun, and Li Jian, Provincial Surveillance Assistant Commissioners, extending also to all the functionaries…

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
事俱遴選屬吏有才行者充
之自鎖院至撤棘試士凡三
歷旬幾二克謙等夙夜殫心
校讐惟明惟慎諸有事於試
院者咸持寅秉哲恪供厥職
務期得人以副
當宁求賢事天之心既取其文
===
之理明氣充者九十人復第
其氏名刻純雅之辭為小錄
仰惟
皇朝膺天眷命奄有萬方建學育
才不遺遐僻
一祖
四宗治教逾百年典禮命討式和
punctuated:
事，俱遴選屬吏有才行者充之。自鎖院至撤棘，試士凡三，歷旬幾二。克謙等夙夜殫心校讐，惟明惟慎。諸有事於試院者，咸持寅秉哲，恪供厥職，務期得人，以副當宁求賢事天之心。既取其文之理明氣充者九十人，復第其氏名，刻純雅之辭為小錄。
仰惟皇朝膺天眷命，奄有萬方，建學育才，不遺遐僻。一祖四宗，治教逾百年，典禮命討，式和
translation_en:
…the various functionaries were all selected from subordinate officials possessing ability and good conduct to fill these duties. From the sealing of the examination compound to the removal of its thorn barriers, the candidates were examined in three sessions, over nearly twenty days. Keqian and his colleagues devoted themselves day and night to evaluating the papers, striving for discernment and care. All those serving in the examination compound maintained reverence and sound judgment and conscientiously discharged their duties. Their aim was to obtain worthy men, fulfilling the reigning sovereign’s desire to seek the worthy and serve Heaven. Having selected ninety men whose compositions displayed clear reasoning and abundant vigor, they then arranged their names in order of merit and engraved their refined and correct writings to form this brief record.
We reverently reflect that our imperial dynasty received Heaven’s favor and mandate and came to possess all lands. It established schools and nurtured talent, neglecting no place, however remote. Under the founding emperor and the four succeeding emperors, government and moral instruction have extended over more than a hundred years. Through prescribed rites and the bestowal of rewards and punishments, they have brought into harmony…

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
民衷仁育義正化洽寰區亦
惟天佑命之純克生多賢用
資佐理
上嗣大寶位十有七年大比賓興
已歷六科近而密勿廟堂若
保傅卿佐若侍從風紀遠而
承流藩服若司府長貳若州
===
邑守令惟科目之賢是重而
中外臣工罔不欽若
皇上憲天聰明之休保乂黎元嘉
靖華夏萬邦黎獻游歌黌序
服詩書禮樂之習為明體適
用之學亦惟發身科目媲美
先達是志矧浙為東南文物
punctuated:
民衷，仁育義正，化洽寰區，亦惟天佑命之純，克生多賢，用資佐理。
上嗣大寶位十有七年，大比賓興已歷六科。近而密勿廟堂，若保傅卿佐，若侍從風紀；遠而承流藩服，若司府長貳，若州邑守令，惟科目之賢是重。而中外臣工罔不欽若皇上憲天聰明之休，保乂黎元，嘉靖華夏。萬邦黎獻游歌黌序，服詩書禮樂之習，為明體適用之學，亦惟發身科目，媲美先達是志。矧浙為東南文物
translation_en:
…the people's innermost dispositions. Through benevolence they nurture, and through righteousness they rectify; their transforming influence pervades the realm. It is also through the purity of Heaven's protecting mandate that so many worthy men have been born to assist in governance.
It has been seventeen years since His Majesty succeeded to the imperial throne, and six rounds of the triennial examinations for honoring and advancing worthy men have already taken place. Whether serving close at hand, diligently engaged at court—as guardians and preceptors, ministers and their assistants, attendants and censors—or serving afar, extending the influence of imperial government throughout the provinces—as heads and deputies of provincial commissions and prefectures, or as magistrates of departments and counties—it is worthy men from the examinations who are esteemed. Officials within and beyond the capital all reverently follow His Majesty's admirable example of modeling his perceptiveness upon Heaven, protecting and governing the common people and bringing peace and order to the Chinese realm. Worthy men throughout the land study and sing in the schools, devote themselves to the Odes, Documents, rites, and music, and pursue learning that illuminates fundamental principles and applies them to practical affairs. Their ambition, too, is to enter official life through the examinations and match the excellence of their distinguished predecessors. All the more so since Zhejiang is a land of cultural refinement in the southeast …

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之邦山川秀淑産毓英才得
雋書名垂聲邁烈者繇昔逮
今彬彬其盛顧惟兹科防範
取舍畢協至公盖不雜以人
為而法乎天道之純誠也諸
士子中式之文根本乎性道
出入乎經史分章乎雲漢志
===
勤而功博夫豈無徵者與故
觀其理明足以驗所學之能
知天觀其氣充足以驗所養
之能事天有學有養庶乎其
盡天降之才矣登名賢書抑
何忝與行將會天下士偕試
春官進敷
punctuated: 之邦，山川秀淑，産毓英才，得雋書名、垂聲邁烈者，繇昔逮今，彬彬其盛。顧惟兹科，防範取舍，畢協至公，盖不雜以人為，而法乎天道之純誠也。諸士子中式之文，根本乎性道，出入乎經史，分章乎雲漢，志勤而功博，夫豈無徵者與？故觀其理明，足以驗所學之能知天；觀其氣充，足以驗所養之能事天。有學有養，庶乎其盡天降之才矣。登名賢書，抑何忝與？行將會天下士，偕試春官，進敷
translation_en: …a land whose beautiful mountains and rivers nurture outstanding talents. From antiquity to the present, those who have distinguished themselves in examinations and had their names inscribed, bequeathing their renown and surpassing others in achievement, have flourished in splendid abundance. In this examination, the safeguards and the decisions to accept or reject candidates have all accorded with the utmost impartiality. They have been free of human contrivance, taking as their model the pure sincerity of the Way of Heaven. The successful candidates’ compositions are rooted in human nature and the Way, range through the classics and histories, and display patterns like the Milky Way [?]. Their aspirations are earnest and their attainments extensive: surely there is evidence of this? Thus, the clarity of their reasoning sufficiently demonstrates that their learning enables them to understand Heaven; the fullness of their vital energy sufficiently demonstrates that their self-cultivation enables them to serve Heaven. Possessing both learning and self-cultivation, they may come close to fully realizing the talents Heaven has bestowed upon them. What cause have they for shame in having their names entered in the register of worthies? Soon they will join scholars from throughout the realm to sit together for the examination conducted by the Ministry of Rites, and advance to present …

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
廷對布列庶位雖所職異事莫
非天理之散殊可幾微少忽
乎其必惕勵朝夕畏天命也
懋脩政教亮天工也弼固
皇圖迓天休也若然則仰不愧俯
不怍而天錫之福民懷其惠
為科目增重必矣書曰慎厥
===
終惟其始諸士子大受遠到
皆始乎發解故敢以是言為
規使定其初志云
山東兗州府儒學教授莆田
王克謙謹序
punctuated:
廷對，布列庶位，雖所職異事，莫非天理之散殊，可幾微少忽乎？其必惕勵朝夕，畏天命也；懋脩政教，亮天工也；弼固皇圖，迓天休也。若然，則仰不愧，俯不怍，而天錫之福，民懷其惠，為科目增重必矣。《書》曰：「慎厥終，惟其始。」諸士子大受遠到，皆始乎發解，故敢以是言為規，使定其初志云。
山東兗州府儒學教授莆田王克謙謹序。
translation_en:
…present their responses at court and take their places in the various offices. Though their official responsibilities concern different affairs, all are diverse manifestations of Heaven’s principle. Can they allow themselves even the slightest negligence? They must remain vigilant and diligent morning and evening, in awe of Heaven’s mandate; strive to cultivate government and moral instruction, assisting Heaven’s work; and uphold and strengthen the imperial realm, welcoming Heaven’s blessings. If they do so, they will feel no shame when looking upward or downward. Heaven will bestow blessings upon them, and the people will cherish their beneficence. They will assuredly add prestige to the examination system. The Book of Documents says: “To be careful of the end, attend to the beginning.” These scholars’ assumption of great responsibilities and attainment of far-reaching achievements all begin with success in the Provincial Examination. Thus I venture to offer these words as an admonition, that they may firmly establish their initial resolve.
Preface respectfully written by Wang Keqian of Putian, Professor of the Confucian School of Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong.

text:

translation_en:
Zhejiang Provincial Examination, the sixteenth year of Chenghua (1480)

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
己欲立而立人己欲達而達人
故君子不可以不脩身思脩身不可以不
事親思事親不可以不知人思知人不可
以不知天天下之達道五所以行之
者三曰君臣也父子也夫婦也昆弟也
朋友之交也五者天下之達道也知仁
勇三者天下之達德也所以行之者一
===
也或生而知之或學而知之或困而知
之及其知之一也或安而行之或利而
行之或勉強而行之及其成功一也子
曰好學近乎知力行近乎仁知恥近乎
勇知斯三者則知所以脩身
鄉田同井出入相友守望相助疾病相扶
持則百姓親睦方里而井井九百畝其
中為公田八家皆私百畝同養公田
易
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

己欲立而立人，己欲達而達人。

故君子不可以不脩身。思脩身，不可以不事親；思事親，不可以不知人；思知人，不可以不知天。天下之達道五，所以行之者三。曰：君臣也，父子也，夫婦也，昆弟也，朋友之交也。五者，天下之達道也。知、仁、勇三者，天下之達德也。所以行之者一也。或生而知之，或學而知之，或困而知之，及其知之，一也。或安而行之，或利而行之，或勉強而行之，及其成功，一也。子曰：「好學近乎知，力行近乎仁，知恥近乎勇。」知斯三者，則知所以脩身。

鄉田同井，出入相友，守望相助，疾病相扶持，則百姓親睦。方里而井，井九百畝，其中為公田。八家皆私百畝，同養公田。

易
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Wishing to establish himself, he establishes others; wishing to attain success himself, he helps others attain success.

Therefore, the gentleman must cultivate himself. Wishing to cultivate himself, he must serve his parents; wishing to serve his parents, he must understand people; wishing to understand people, he must understand Heaven. There are five universal relationships under Heaven, and three virtues by which they are put into practice. These relationships are those between ruler and minister, father and son, husband and wife, elder and younger brothers, and friends. These five are the universal relationships under Heaven. Wisdom, benevolence, and courage are the three universal virtues under Heaven. That by which they are put into practice is one. Some understand them from birth, some through study, and some through struggling with difficulties; once they understand them, the understanding is the same. Some practice them naturally, some for their benefit, and some through strenuous effort; once they achieve success, the result is the same. The Master said: “Love of learning approaches wisdom; vigorous practice approaches benevolence; knowing shame approaches courage.” Knowing these three, one knows how to cultivate oneself.

When those farming the countryside share the same well-field, accompany one another when going out and returning, help one another in keeping watch, and support one another in illness, the common people will live in affection and harmony. A square measuring one li on each side forms a well-field of nine hundred mu, with the public field at its center. Each of eight households has one hundred mu for its own use, and all jointly cultivate the public field.

Book of Changes

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
謙尊而光卑而不可踰君子之終也象曰
地中有山謙君子以裒多益寡稱物平
施
利見大人亨利貞
大衍之數五十其用四十有九分而為二
以象兩掛一以象三揲之以四以象四
時歸奇於扐以象閏五歲再閏故再扐
而後掛乾之策二百一十有六坤之策
百四十有四凡三百有六十當期之日
===
二篇之策萬有一千五百二十當萬物
之數也是故四營而成易十有八變而
成卦八卦而小成引而伸之觸類而長
之天下之能事畢矣
夫乾確然示人易矣夫坤隤然示人簡矣
爻也者效此者也象也者像此者也爻
象動乎内吉凶見乎外功業見乎變聖
人之情見乎辭天地之大德曰生聖人
之大寶曰位何以守位曰仁何以聚人
punctuated:
謙，尊而光，卑而不可踰，君子之終也。象曰：「地中有山，謙。君子以裒多益寡，稱物平施。」
利見大人，亨，利貞。
大衍之數五十，其用四十有九。分而為二以象兩，掛一以象三，揲之以四以象四時，歸奇於扐以象閏。五歲再閏，故再扐而後掛。乾之策二百一十有六，坤之策百四十有四，凡三百有六十，當期之日。二篇之策萬有一千五百二十，當萬物之數也。是故四營而成易，十有八變而成卦。八卦而小成，引而伸之，觸類而長之，天下之能事畢矣。
夫乾，確然示人易矣；夫坤，隤然示人簡矣。爻也者，效此者也；象也者，像此者也。爻象動乎内，吉凶見乎外，功業見乎變，聖人之情見乎辭。天地之大德曰生，聖人之大寶曰位。何以守位？曰仁。何以聚人？
translation_en:
…Modesty brings radiance to those in high station and makes those in low station impossible to overstep. This is the culmination of the noble person’s conduct. The Image commentary says: “Within the earth is a mountain: Modesty. The noble person accordingly reduces what is excessive and augments what is deficient, weighing things and distributing them equitably.”
It is favorable to see the great man. Success. It is favorable to remain steadfast.
The number of the Great Expansion is fifty; of these, forty-nine are used. Divide them into two groups to symbolize the two primal powers; set one stalk apart between the fingers to symbolize the three powers; count off the stalks in fours to symbolize the four seasons; place the remainder between the fingers to symbolize an intercalary month. There are two intercalations in five years; therefore, place remainders between the fingers twice before again setting one stalk apart. The stalk total for Qian is two hundred and sixteen; that for Kun is one hundred and forty-four. Together they make three hundred and sixty, corresponding to the days of a year. The stalk total for the two parts of the Book of Changes is eleven thousand five hundred and twenty, corresponding to the number of the myriad things. Thus four operations complete one change, and eighteen changes complete a hexagram. The eight trigrams constitute a lesser completion. By drawing them out and extending them, and expanding them through analogous cases, all that can be accomplished under Heaven is encompassed.
Qian, firm and unyielding, shows people ease; Kun, yielding and compliant, shows people simplicity. The lines imitate these; the images represent these. The lines and images move within, and good and ill fortune appear without. Accomplishments appear in the transformations, and the dispositions of the sages appear in the statements. The great virtue of Heaven and Earth is called generation; the great treasure of the sage is called position. By what does he preserve his position? Benevolence. By what does he gather the people? …

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
曰財理財正辭禁民為非曰義
書
肇十有二州封十有二山濬川象以典刑
流宥五刑鞭作官刑扑作教刑金作贖
刑
浮于江沱潜漢逾于洛至于南河
貳公弘化寅亮天地
德威惟畏德明惟明乃命三后恤功于民
伯夷降典折民惟刑禹平水土主名山
===
川稷降播種農殖嘉穀三后成功惟殷
于民士制百姓于刑之中以教祇德穆
穆在上明明在下灼于四方罔不惟德
之勤故乃明于刑之中率乂于民棐彝
詩
我徂東山慆慆不歸我來自東零雨其濛
我東曰歸我心西悲制彼裳衣勿士行
枚蜎蜎者蠋烝在桑野敦彼獨宿亦在
車下
punctuated:
曰財。理財、正辭、禁民為非，曰義。

書

肇十有二州，封十有二山，濬川。象以典刑，流宥五刑，鞭作官刑，扑作教刑，金作贖刑。

浮于江、沱、潜、漢，逾于洛，至于南河。

貳公弘化，寅亮天地。

德威惟畏，德明惟明。乃命三后，恤功于民：伯夷降典，折民惟刑；禹平水土，主名山川；稷降播種，農殖嘉穀。三后成功，惟殷于民。士制百姓于刑之中，以教祇德。穆穆在上，明明在下，灼于四方，罔不惟德之勤。故乃明于刑之中，率乂于民，棐彝。

詩

我徂東山，慆慆不歸。我來自東，零雨其濛。我東曰歸，我心西悲。制彼裳衣，勿士行枚。蜎蜎者蠋，烝在桑野。敦彼獨宿，亦在車下。
translation_en:
…The answer is wealth. Managing wealth, rectifying speech, and forbidding the people to do wrong are called righteousness.

Book of Documents

He first established twelve provinces, designated twelve mountains as their principal mountains, and dredged the rivers. He set forth the regular punishments, allowing exile to mitigate the five punishments; the whip served as punishment for officials, the rod as punishment in education, and payments in metal as redemption from punishment.

They traveled by water along the Jiang, Tuo, Qian, and Han rivers, crossed over to the Luo, and reached the southern stretch of the Yellow River.

Assist the Grand Dukes in spreading transforming instruction; reverently aid the ordering of Heaven and Earth.

The awe inspired by virtue alone is truly awe-inspiring; the illumination of virtue alone is truly enlightening. He therefore charged three lords to undertake works for the people's welfare. Bo Yi promulgated the statutes, guiding the people by proper standards; Yu brought the waters and lands into order and took charge of the principal mountains and rivers; Ji taught sowing and planting, cultivating fine grains. The three lords accomplished their work, bringing abundance to the people. The Director of Justice regulated the hundred families through the proper application of punishments, teaching them to revere virtue. Majestic above and discerning below, their influence shone throughout the four quarters, and none failed to strive for virtue. Thus they understood the proper application of punishments, led the people into good order, and upheld the constant moral norms.

Book of Odes

I went away to the eastern hills,
And for so long did not return.
Now I come back from the east;
The falling rain is misty.
When word came in the east that we would return,
My heart grieved, yearning westward.
Make those everyday clothes;
No longer serve with a marching gag in the mouth.
The wriggling caterpillar
Lies out in the mulberry fields.
Curled up, sleeping alone,
I too lie beneath a cart.

translation_en:
Heaven protects and establishes you, making you very secure. It grants you abundant bounty: what blessing does it not bestow? It grants you increase in all things, so that nothing fails to flourish. Heaven protects and establishes you, granting you happiness and good fortune. Everything is fitting; you receive Heaven’s hundred blessings. It sends down lasting blessings upon you, as though the days were insufficient for them. Heaven protects and establishes you, so that nothing fails to prosper. Like mountains and hills, like ridges and lofty mounds, like a river’s swelling flow, nothing fails to increase.

Numerous and dignified are the many worthy men; through them King Wen enjoys peace.

Sharp are the fine ploughshares as work begins in the southern fields. They sow the hundred grains; the seeds hold life and sprout. Someone comes to visit you, carrying square and round baskets. title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
有虞氏之祭也尚用氣血腥燖祭用氣也
殷人尚聲臭味未成滌蕩其聲樂三闋
然後出迎牲聲音之號所以詔告於天
地之間也周人尚臭灌用鬯臭鬱合鬯
臭陰達於淵泉灌以圭璋用玉氣也既
灌然後迎牲致陰氣也蕭合黍稷臭陽
達於墻屋故既奠然後爇蕭合羶薌凡
祭慎諸此
君子如欲化民成俗其必由學乎玉不琢
===
不成器人不學不知道是故古之王者
建國君民教學為先
禮樂明備天地官矣
言而履之禮也行而樂之樂也君子力此
二者以南面而立夫是以天下大平也
諸侯朝萬物服體而百官莫敢不承事
矣
第貳場
論
punctuated:
有虞氏之祭也，尚用氣。血腥燖祭，用氣也。殷人尚聲，臭味未成，滌蕩其聲，樂三闋，然後出迎牲。聲音之號，所以詔告於天地之間也。周人尚臭，灌用鬯，臭鬱合鬯，臭陰達於淵泉。灌以圭璋，用玉氣也。既灌，然後迎牲，致陰氣也。蕭合黍稷，臭陽達於墻屋。故既奠，然後爇蕭，合羶薌。凡祭，慎諸此。
君子如欲化民成俗，其必由學乎！玉不琢，不成器；人不學，不知道。是故古之王者，建國君民，教學為先。
禮樂明備，天地官矣。
言而履之，禮也；行而樂之，樂也。君子力此二者，以南面而立。夫是以天下大平也，諸侯朝，萬物服體，而百官莫敢不承事矣。
第貳場
論
translation_en:
In the sacrifices of the house of Yu, emphasis was placed on using vital emanations. Offering blood, raw flesh, and scalded flesh made use of these emanations. The people of Yin valued sound. Before the scents and flavors were fully prepared, they made their music resound; after three musical performances, they went out to receive the sacrificial animal. The proclamation made through sound served to announce the sacrifice throughout heaven and earth. The people of Zhou valued scent. For the libation they used aromatic millet wine, blending fragrant yu herbs into it; its scent descended through the yin realm to the deep springs. They poured the libation using gui and zhang jade vessels, employing the emanations of jade. After the libation, they received the sacrificial animal, thereby bringing forth the yin emanations. Southernwood was combined with glutinous and non-glutinous millet, and its scent rose through the yang realm to the walls and roofs. Thus, after setting out the offerings, they burned southernwood, combining it with fragrant fat and grain. In every sacrifice, careful attention was paid to these matters.
If a gentleman wishes to transform the people and establish good customs, must he not do so through learning? Unless jade is carved, it does not become a vessel; unless a person studies, he does not understand the Way. Therefore, when the kings of antiquity founded states and ruled their people, they gave priority to teaching and learning.
When rites and music are clearly established and complete, heaven and earth fulfill their appointed functions.
To put one's words into practice is ritual; to take delight in one's conduct is music. The gentleman diligently applies himself to these two things and takes his place facing south as ruler. Through this, all under heaven enjoys great peace: the regional lords come to court, all beings submit in their persons, and none of the officials dares fail to perform his duties.
Second Session
Discourse

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
五教是已下至漢唐宋姑未暇論洪惟
我
太祖高皇帝肇造區夏御製大誥三編訓飭臣
民
太宗文皇帝輯寧邦家御製為善陰隲孝順事
實二書以勉人為善為孝
宣宗章皇帝繼體守成御製五倫一書以教人
明倫觀大誥所載或彰善以示勸而其
所彰者何人或癉惡以示懲而其所癉
===
者何人為善陰隲所載有不妄殺一人
而其女為后者有辯孝婦之冤而後昆
以興者誰歟孝順事實所載有負罪引
慝克諧以孝者有一日三朝而問安視
膳者又誰歟至若五倫書所載有生而
神靈弱而能言見於聖德篇者何君有
慎厥身脩思永后從諫則聖見於輔德
篇者何臣他如篤父子之恩有三見三
笞負米百里者全夫婦之別有釐降溈
punctuated: 五教是已。下至漢唐宋，姑未暇論。洪惟我太祖高皇帝肇造區夏，御製《大誥》三編，訓飭臣民。太宗文皇帝輯寧邦家，御製《為善陰隲》《孝順事實》二書，以勉人為善、為孝。宣宗章皇帝繼體守成，御製《五倫》一書，以教人明倫。觀《大誥》所載，或彰善以示勸，而其所彰者何人？或癉惡以示懲，而其所癉者何人？《為善陰隲》所載，有不妄殺一人而其女為后者，有辯孝婦之冤而後昆以興者，誰歟？《孝順事實》所載，有負罪引慝、克諧以孝者，有一日三朝而問安視膳者，又誰歟？至若《五倫》書所載，有生而神靈、弱而能言，見於《聖德》篇者，何君？有「慎厥身，脩思永」「后從諫則聖」，見於《輔德》篇者，何臣？他如篤父子之恩，有三見三笞、負米百里者；全夫婦之別，有釐降溈
translation_en:
…these were the five teachings. As for the later Han, Tang, and Song dynasties, we shall for the moment leave them undiscussed. We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao founded the realm and personally composed the three compilations of the Grand Pronouncements (Da Gao) to instruct and admonish officials and commoners. Emperor Taizong Wen brought peace to the state and personally composed Doing Good and Hidden Recompense (Weishan Yinzhi) and Accounts of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun Shishi) to encourage people to practice goodness and filial piety. Emperor Xuanzong Zhang succeeded to the throne and preserved the achievements of his predecessors; he personally composed the Five Relationships (Wulun) to teach people to understand human relationships.

Looking at what is recorded in the Grand Pronouncements, some passages commend goodness to encourage others: who are those commended? Others denounce wickedness to serve as a warning: who are those denounced? Among those recorded in Doing Good and Hidden Recompense, there is one who did not wantonly put a single person to death and whose daughter became empress, and another who vindicated a filial woman unjustly accused and whose descendants subsequently prospered. Who were they? Among those recorded in Accounts of Filial Obedience, there is one who took the blame and acknowledged faults, achieving harmony through filial piety, and another who attended his parent three times a day, inquiring after his health and overseeing his meals. Who, again, were they?

As for those recorded in the Five Relationships, which ruler was possessed of divine intelligence from birth and able to speak in infancy, as recounted in the chapter “Sagely Virtue”? Which ministers spoke the words “Be watchful over your person; cultivate yourself with thoughts for the long term” and “A sovereign who follows remonstrance becomes a sage,” as recounted in the chapter “Assisting Virtue”? Among others who deepened the affection between father and son, there are those who were seen three times and beaten three times [?], and who carried rice a hundred li. Among those who maintained the distinction between husband and wife, there is the account of giving daughters in marriage at the Gui…

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
汭娶瞽不貳者又有自縛詣賊免弟於
難遇盜請代脫兄於烹而全兄弟之恩
者一入京師見者嘆服一扣所學稱為
老友而篤朋友之倫者凡此皆可指其
人而言歟
列聖之立言垂訓其與堯舜禹湯文武之克綏
厥猷果同一揆歟諸生佩服有年不知
處於家達於官果以何人為法歟幸明
言之毋隱
===
問張子西銘先儒謂訂頑之言極純無雜
又謂訂頑一篇乃仁之體又曰西銘為
原道之宗祖又曰觀子厚所作西銘能
養浩然之氣者可詳言其義歟程門弟
子有半載後方得看者有往復書辯終
未釋然者何為其然歟紫陽朱子又謂
西銘前一段如棋盤後一段如人下棋
所謂如棋盤者何所指所謂如人下棋
者何所該又謂西銘有箇直劈下底道
punctuated:
汭、娶瞽不貳者；又有自縛詣賊，免弟於難，遇盜請代，脫兄於烹，而全兄弟之恩者；一入京師，見者嘆服，一扣所學，稱為老友，而篤朋友之倫者。凡此皆可指其人而言歟？列聖之立言垂訓，其與堯舜禹湯文武之克綏厥猷，果同一揆歟？諸生佩服有年，不知處於家、達於官，果以何人為法歟？幸明言之，毋隱。

問：張子《西銘》，先儒謂「訂頑之言，極純無雜」，又謂「訂頑一篇，乃仁之體」，又曰「西銘為原道之宗祖」，又曰「觀子厚所作西銘，能養浩然之氣者」。可詳言其義歟？程門弟子，有半載後方得看者，有往復書辯終未釋然者，何為其然歟？紫陽朱子又謂：「西銘前一段如棋盤，後一段如人下棋。」所謂如棋盤者何所指？所謂如人下棋者何所該？又謂西銘有箇直劈下底道
translation_en:
…the bend of the Gui River, and one who married a blind woman and remained faithful to her; there were also those who bound themselves and went before rebels to save a younger brother from danger, or, encountering bandits, asked to take an elder brother’s place and saved him from being boiled alive, thereby preserving the affection between brothers. There were those who, upon entering the capital, won the admiration of all who saw them, or who, once questioned about their learning, were hailed as old friends, thereby strengthening the bonds of friendship. Can you identify all these people and discuss them?

When our successive sage emperors set forth their teachings for posterity, did they indeed follow the same guiding principle as Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu in bringing their way into peaceful order? You students have revered and upheld these teachings for years. Whether living at home or advancing to official service, whom, in fact, do you take as your model? Please state this clearly and conceal nothing.

Question: Concerning Master Zhang’s Western Inscription (Ximing), earlier Confucian scholars said, “The words of Correcting Obstinacy (Dingwan) are utterly pure and unmixed”; also, “The essay Correcting Obstinacy embodies benevolence”; also, “The Western Inscription is the progenitor of Inquiry into the Way (Yuandao)”; and also, “Reading the Western Inscription composed by Zihou can nourish one’s vast, overflowing vital energy.” Can you explain these statements in detail? Among the disciples of Master Cheng, there was one who was allowed to read it only after half a year, and another who exchanged letters debating it but never fully resolved his doubts. Why was this so?

Master Zhu of Ziyang further said, “The first section of the Western Inscription is like a game board; the latter section is like someone playing on it.” What does the comparison to a game board refer to? What does the comparison to someone playing encompass? He also said that the Western Inscription contains a principle that cleaves straight downward…

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
理又有一箇横截斷底道理推親親之
厚以大無我之公因事親之誠以明事
天之道何以見其然歟抑有一言以盖
其義歟盍著于篇以觀窮理之學
問古者國家雖安尤必擇將傳曰君不擇
將以其國與敵也然擇將之道惟審其
才之可用不以遠而遺不以賤而棄不
以詐而疏不以罪而廢自古為將而起
於疏賤寒微罪累者可歷數其人歟凡
===
選將以五材為體五謹為用而五材五
謹之目可悉數歟將有五危六敗九術
十過又有外貌十五不與衆情相應而
知之有八徵之法者皆可得而舉歟說
者謂將固貴乎能選而尤貴乎能用古
之帝王負知人之明得用將之道往往
命將出師而獲豐功偉蹟昭在簡冊享
祀無窮者多矣可歷指而言歟諸生強
學待問於茲有年願明以告我將獻之
punctuated:
理，又有一箇横截斷底道理。推親親之厚，以大無我之公；因事親之誠，以明事天之道。何以見其然歟？抑有一言以盖其義歟？盍著于篇，以觀窮理之學？
問：古者國家雖安，尤必擇將。傳曰：「君不擇將，以其國與敵也。」然擇將之道，惟審其才之可用，不以遠而遺，不以賤而棄，不以詐而疏，不以罪而廢。自古為將而起於疏賤寒微罪累者，可歷數其人歟？凡選將，以五材為體，五謹為用，而五材五謹之目，可悉數歟？將有五危、六敗、九術、十過，又有外貌十五不與衆情相應，而知之有八徵之法者，皆可得而舉歟？說者謂將固貴乎能選，而尤貴乎能用。古之帝王，負知人之明，得用將之道，往往命將出師，而獲豐功偉蹟，昭在簡冊，享祀無窮者多矣。可歷指而言歟？諸生強學待問，於茲有年，願明以告我，將獻之
translation_en:
…principle, and also a principle that cuts straight across horizontally. Extend the depth of affection for one’s kin to enlarge the impartiality that admits no selfishness; through sincerity in serving one’s parents, illuminate the Way of serving Heaven. How can these claims be demonstrated? Is there perhaps a single statement that encompasses their meaning? Set this out in an essay, so that we may observe your learning in the investigation of principle.
Question: In antiquity, even when the state was at peace, it was still essential to select its generals carefully. A transmitted text says: “A ruler who does not select his generals carefully hands his state over to the enemy.” The method of selecting generals consists solely in judging whether their abilities can be put to use: do not overlook a man because he is distant, reject him because he is lowly, keep him at a distance because he is deceitful, or discard him because he has committed an offense. Can you enumerate the men who, from antiquity onward, became generals after rising from obscurity, humble status, poverty, or the burden of criminal offenses? In selecting generals, the five talents constitute the foundation, and the five precautions govern their application. Can you enumerate all the items comprising these five talents and five precautions? For generals there are five dangers, six defeats, nine techniques, and ten faults. There are also fifteen outward appearances that do not correspond to underlying dispositions [?], and a method of eight tests by which to discern them. Can you set all these out? Commentators say that, although the ability to select generals is certainly valuable, the ability to employ them is still more valuable. Among the emperors and kings of antiquity, many possessed the discernment to understand men and mastered the method of employing generals. Time and again they appointed generals to lead armies into the field and achieved great accomplishments and mighty deeds, recorded illustriously in the histories, and received sacrificial offerings without end. Can you identify and discuss them one by one? You students have studied diligently and prepared to answer questions for years now. I hope you will explain these matters clearly to me; I shall present your answers to…

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
聖明用備採擇焉
問江浙古揚州之域今為天下冠冕之藩
其間人物卓異不可以偪指盡也試舉
其槩與諸士子評之有自誓以四勿者
有君稱其五絕者有與商山四皓之列
者有居儒林四傑之班者有號二樓二
肅者有目三劉三方者可得而條陳歟
有治富春加右大將軍者有守會稽徵
為主爵都尉者有遷合浦守人稱神明
===
者有為黃巖尉人稱鐵面少府者有見
爭義公封還內降者有彈劾奸欺賦詩
愛民者可得而歷舉歟何才稱以李白
何才稱以不羈息牂牁之疑乞侂冑之
誅者誰歟斥蔡京逆豫之罪罵縉雲雎
陽之賊者誰歟武康何人也昌黎見其
人引為忘年之交天台何人也徽宗覽
其詩嘆其得見之晚獲稱於朱晦庵者
一載於像贊一載於景行堂記可撮其
punctuated:
聖明，用備採擇焉。
問：江浙，古揚州之域，今為天下冠冕之藩。其間人物卓異，不可以偪指盡也。試舉其槩，與諸士子評之。有自誓以四勿者，有君稱其五絕者，有與商山四皓之列者，有居儒林四傑之班者，有號二樓二肅者，有目三劉三方者，可得而條陳歟？有治富春加右大將軍者，有守會稽徵為主爵都尉者，有遷合浦守人稱神明者，有為黃巖尉人稱鐵面少府者，有見爭義公封還內降者，有彈劾奸欺賦詩愛民者，可得而歷舉歟？何才稱以李白？何才稱以不羈？息牂牁之疑、乞侂冑之誅者，誰歟？斥蔡京、逆豫之罪，罵縉雲、雎陽之賊者，誰歟？武康何人也，昌黎見其人，引為忘年之交？天台何人也，徽宗覽其詩，嘆其得見之晚？獲稱於朱晦庵者，一載於像贊，一載於景行堂記，可撮其
translation_en:
…to His Sagacious Majesty, for his consideration and selection.
Question: Jiangsu and Zhejiang lie within the territory of ancient Yangzhou and now constitute the foremost region of the realm. Their outstanding figures are too numerous to count on one’s fingers. Let us offer a general selection for discussion with you candidates. There was one who bound himself by an oath to the Four Prohibitions; one whose Five Excellences his ruler praised; one who belonged among the Four Hoary Elders of Mount Shang; and one who ranked among the Four Outstanding Scholars of the Confucian community. There were those called the Two Lous and the Two Sus, and those known as the Three Lius and the Three Fangs. Can you set them out individually?
There was one who governed Fuchun and received the additional title of Grand General of the Right; one who governed Kuaiji and was summoned to become Chief Commandant for Nobility; one who was transferred to serve as governor of Hepu and whom the people called divinely perceptive; and one who served as district defender of Huangyan and whom the people called the Iron-faced Lesser Treasurer. There was one associated with “contending for righteousness, my lord” [?] who sealed and returned an order issued from within the palace; and one who impeached deceitful wrongdoers and composed poems expressing love for the people. Can you enumerate them in turn?
Whose talent earned comparison with Li Bai? Whose talent was described as untrammeled? Who dispelled the doubts concerning Zangke, and who petitioned for Tuozhou’s execution? Who denounced the crimes of Cai Jing and the rebel Yu, and who reviled the bandits of Jinyun and Juyang [?]? Who was the man of Wukang whom Changli, upon meeting him, took as a friend despite their difference in age? Who was the man of Tiantai whose poems Huizong read, lamenting that he had encountered him so late? Of those praised by Zhu Hui’an, one is recorded in a portrait encomium and another in the Record of Jingxing Hall. Can you summarize their …

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
畧歎見詠於李忠定張公祐者一為戮
賊擢爵一為清節愈堅可指其實歟封
禪無書何人有是隱逸晚節勇退何人
有是恬靜徴召之屢若可就也寧破琴
不彈何心耶尊禮之勤若可屈也寧一
絲獨釣何意耶之數君子皆爾浙中人
物必有景慕而願法之者其歷言之以
觀尚友之學
問窮經將以致用識時在於俊傑試以時
===
務一二相與折衷之且如兩浙素稱富
庶之邦而專水陸之利近年以來民窮
財匱或曰習尚過於侈靡或曰徵斂傷
於頻煩孰為確論浙東之地多高不宜
久晴浙西之地多卑不宜久雨稍遇水
旱民輙告災欲施賑濟之條則恐公廩
已乏陳餘欲舉勸分之典則恐私家亦
無畜積何為良法又聞沿海軍士粮餉
有缺雖給府庫羨財慮恐後難相繼錢
punctuated:
畧歎？見詠於李忠定、張公祐者，一為戮賊擢爵，一為清節愈堅，可指其實歟？封禪無書，何人有是隱逸？晚節勇退，何人有是恬靜？徴召之屢，若可就也，寧破琴不彈，何心耶？尊禮之勤，若可屈也，寧一絲獨釣，何意耶？之數君子，皆爾浙中人物，必有景慕而願法之者。其歷言之，以觀尚友之學。
問：窮經將以致用，識時在於俊傑。試以時務一二，相與折衷之。且如兩浙素稱富庶之邦，而專水陸之利，近年以來，民窮財匱。或曰習尚過於侈靡，或曰徵斂傷於頻煩，孰為確論？浙東之地多高，不宜久晴；浙西之地多卑，不宜久雨。稍遇水旱，民輙告災。欲施賑濟之條，則恐公廩已乏陳餘；欲舉勸分之典，則恐私家亦無畜積。何為良法？又聞沿海軍士粮餉有缺，雖給府庫羨財，慮恐後難相繼。錢
translation_en:
…an outline [?]? Of those celebrated in verse by Li Zhongding and Zhang Gongyou, one received advancement in noble rank for slaying rebels, while the other grew ever firmer in his unsullied integrity. Can you specify the facts? Who displayed such reclusive independence by writing nothing on the Feng and Shan sacrifices? Who displayed such serenity by resolutely retiring in his later years? Repeated summons might seemingly have induced one to take office, yet he preferred to break his zither and cease playing: what was his intention? Assiduous honors and courtesies might seemingly have induced another to yield, yet he preferred to fish alone with a single line: what did he mean? These gentlemen were all figures from your own Zhejiang; surely there are some whom you admire and wish to emulate. Discuss them one by one, so that we may assess your learning in befriending the worthy of the past.
Question: Thorough study of the Classics is intended to enable their practical application; understanding the times is the mark of outstanding men. Let us consider one or two current affairs and arrive together at a sound judgment. The Two Zhe regions have long been renowned for wealth and abundance, enjoying exceptional advantages by land and water. Yet in recent years the people have become impoverished and resources depleted. Some say that customary practices have become excessively extravagant; others say that taxation and exactions have caused harm through their frequency. Which is the sound judgment? Much of eastern Zhejiang is high ground and cannot withstand prolonged dry weather; much of western Zhejiang is low ground and cannot withstand prolonged rain. At the slightest flood or drought, the people report a disaster. If we wish to implement relief measures, we fear that the public granaries have no reserves left from previous years. If we wish to invoke the established practice of encouraging the sharing of grain, we fear that private households likewise have no stores. What would be an effective method? We also hear that the coastal soldiers lack grain and pay. Although surplus treasury funds have been provided, there is concern that such support will be difficult to sustain. Qian…

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
塘地方隄堰日坍雖委有司專理慮恐
卒難成功今欲使富庶復舊倉廩有儲
隄堰能久軍無愁嗟民免勞役必有鑿
鑿可行者幸為我言將采而告之當道
者
punctuated: 塘地方隄堰日坍，雖委有司專理，慮恐卒難成功。今欲使富庶復舊，倉廩有儲，隄堰能久，軍無愁嗟，民免勞役，必有鑿鑿可行者，幸為我言，將采而告之當道者。
translation_en: …in the Qiantang area, dikes and weirs crumble daily. Although the responsible officials have been charged specifically with their maintenance, there is concern that success may ultimately prove elusive. Now, to restore the former prosperity, ensure that granaries hold reserves, make dikes and weirs endure, free the soldiers from distress and lamentation, and spare the people corvée labor, there must surely be concrete, practicable measures. Please set them forth for me; I shall adopt them and present them to those in authority.

text:
四書
己欲立而立人己欲達而達人
侯聘
同考試官教諭李批題用揭書出所以杜僥倖也
此作能以內外立說深合本旨
考試官教授徐批說出仁者之心是用錄出
考試官教授王批辭順理明可取
以己所欲而及於人此仁者之心也盖仁者之
心一天理之周流也曾何以所欲而有間於人
===
己哉昔吾夫子因子貢以博施濟衆為仁故狀
仁之體以告之若謂內焉而身之脩外焉而居
之安皆所謂立也是己之所欲亦人之所欲也
但自私者惟欲自立而已烏能立人哉仁者之
心渾然天理而物我無間己欲立也即以立人
手以扶持之培植之而無忌克詆毁之私使之
亦得以自立而囿于吾仁之中焉內焉而理無
不通外焉而行無不得皆所謂達也是己之所
欲亦人之所欲也但自私者惟欲自達而已烏
punctuated:
四書
「己欲立而立人，己欲達而達人。」
侯聘
同考試官教諭李批：「題用揭書出，所以杜僥倖也。此作能以內外立說，深合本旨。」
考試官教授徐批：「說出仁者之心，是用錄出。」
考試官教授王批：「辭順理明，可取。」
以己所欲而及於人，此仁者之心也。盖仁者之心，一天理之周流也，曾何以所欲而有間於人己哉？昔吾夫子因子貢以博施濟衆為仁，故狀仁之體以告之。若謂內焉而身之脩，外焉而居之安，皆所謂立也，是己之所欲，亦人之所欲也。但自私者惟欲自立而已，烏能立人哉？仁者之心，渾然天理，而物我無間。己欲立也，即以立人，手以扶持之、培植之，而無忌克詆毁之私，使之亦得以自立，而囿于吾仁之中焉。內焉而理無不通，外焉而行無不得，皆所謂達也，是己之所欲，亦人之所欲也。但自私者惟欲自達而已，烏
translation_en:
Four Books
“Desiring to establish himself, he establishes others; desiring to attain fulfillment himself, he enables others to attain fulfillment.”
Hou Pin
Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “The topic was selected by opening the book [?], in order to prevent success through lucky guessing. This composition develops its argument through the internal and external aspects, closely matching the original meaning.”
Examiner Xu, Professor, comments: “It brings out the heart of the humane person; for this reason it has been selected for inclusion.”
Examiner Wang, Professor, comments: “The language is fluent and the reasoning clear. It merits acceptance.”
To extend to others what one desires for oneself: this is the heart of the humane person. For the heart of the humane person is nothing other than the all-pervading circulation of Heavenly Principle. How could there be any division between others and oneself in what one desires? In former times, because Zigong took the broad bestowal of benefits and assistance to the multitude to constitute humaneness, our Master described the essential character of humaneness to instruct him. It was as though he were saying: internally, the cultivation of oneself, and externally, security in one’s circumstances—these are both what is meant by being established. This is what one desires for oneself, and what others desire as well. Yet selfish people desire only to establish themselves. How could they establish others?
The heart of the humane person is wholly Heavenly Principle, without division between self and other. Desiring to establish himself, he accordingly establishes others, supporting and nurturing them [手以: doubtful transcription], without selfish jealousy, intolerance, or disparagement. He thus enables them also to establish themselves and to be encompassed within his humaneness. Internally, leaving no principle uncomprehended, and externally, finding success in every action—these are both what is meant by attaining fulfillment. This is what one desires for oneself, and what others desire as well. Yet selfish people desire only to attain fulfillment themselves. How could they…

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
能達人哉仁者之心廓然大公而人己一致己
欲達也即以達人于以開導之汲引之而無遏
塞沮抑之心使之亦得以自達而域於吾仁之
內焉是則立不自立而與人同立達不自達而
與人俱達於此觀之可以見天理之周流而無
間矣狀仁之體孰切於是哉抑合是章論之博
施濟衆仁之極功聖人所難能也立人達人安
行此仁學者未易能也能近取譬強恕求仁學
者所可能也子貢以博施濟衆為仁愈難而愈
===
遠矣使能因聖教而求諸己焉將必由所可能
而進雖所難能者亦由是而可馴致矣苟志於
仁者可不深思而靜體之哉
故君子不可以不脩身思脩身不可以不事
親思事親不可以不知人思知人不可以
不知天天下之達道五所以行之者三曰
君臣也父子也夫婦也昆弟也朋友之交
也五者天下之達道也知仁勇三者天下
之達德也所以行之者一也或生而知之
punctuated:
能達人哉？仁者之心廓然大公，而人己一致。己欲達也，即以達人，于以開導之、汲引之，而無遏塞沮抑之心，使之亦得以自達，而域於吾仁之內焉。是則立不自立，而與人同立；達不自達，而與人俱達。於此觀之，可以見天理之周流而無間矣。狀仁之體，孰切於是哉？抑合是章論之，博施濟衆，仁之極功，聖人所難能也；立人達人，安行此仁，學者未易能也；能近取譬，強恕求仁，學者所可能也。子貢以博施濟衆為仁，愈難而愈遠矣。使能因聖教而求諸己焉，將必由所可能而進，雖所難能者，亦由是而可馴致矣。苟志於仁者，可不深思而靜體之哉？
故君子不可以不脩身。思脩身，不可以不事親；思事親，不可以不知人；思知人，不可以不知天。天下之達道五，所以行之者三。曰：君臣也，父子也，夫婦也，昆弟也，朋友之交也。五者，天下之達道也。知、仁、勇三者，天下之達德也。所以行之者一也。或生而知之，
translation_en:
…how could they enable others to attain fulfillment? The benevolent person's heart is expansive and wholly impartial, treating others and oneself as one. Wishing to attain fulfillment oneself, one therefore enables others to attain it, guiding and advancing them without any intention of obstructing or suppressing them, so that they too may attain fulfillment for themselves and be encompassed within one's benevolence. Thus, in establishing oneself, one does not stand alone but stands together with others; in attaining fulfillment, one does not attain it alone but together with others. Viewed in this light, the unimpeded circulation of Heaven's principle becomes apparent. What could more aptly describe the essential nature of benevolence?
Considering this chapter as a whole, broadly bestowing benefits and aiding the multitude is the highest achievement of benevolence, something even a sage finds difficult to accomplish. Establishing others and enabling them to attain fulfillment, practicing this benevolence with ease, is something learners cannot readily accomplish. Drawing analogies from what is close at hand, striving to practice reciprocity in pursuit of benevolence, is something learners can accomplish. Zigong takes broadly bestowing benefits and aiding the multitude to constitute benevolence, making it ever more difficult and remote. If he could follow the sage's teaching and seek it within himself, he would surely advance from what he can accomplish; even what is difficult to accomplish could thereby be gradually attained. Can anyone who aspires to benevolence fail to ponder this deeply and quietly embody it?
Therefore, the gentleman cannot neglect cultivating himself. Wishing to cultivate himself, he cannot neglect serving his parents; wishing to serve his parents, he cannot neglect understanding people; wishing to understand people, he cannot neglect understanding Heaven. There are five universally applicable ways under Heaven, and three virtues by which they are practiced. These ways concern ruler and minister, father and son, husband and wife, elder and younger brothers, and relations between friends. These five are the universally applicable ways under Heaven. Wisdom, benevolence, and courage: these three are the universally applicable virtues under Heaven. That by which they are practiced is one. Some know them from birth…

詳其所以脩身之事而結其意焉抑何以使人
知所從入也哉中庸述孔子荅哀公問政而言
及此意謂為政在人取人以身故君子不可以
不脩身脩身以道脩道以仁故思脩身不可以
punctuated:
或學而知之，或困而知之，及其知之，一也。或安而行之，或利而行之，或勉強而行之，及其成功，一也。子曰：「好學近乎知，力行近乎仁，知恥近乎勇。知斯三者，則知所以脩身。」

俞穩

同考試官訓導唐批：始終以脩身立說，僅見此篇。
同考試官教諭吳批：長題文字，不假贅詞，此作斂煩就簡，而首尾照應，真作家也。
同考試官教諭謝批：說理明白，措詞簡當，可取。
考試官教授徐批：理明文暢，可取。
考試官教授王批：題長而包括無遺，佳作也。

《中庸》原君子脩身之有本，必詳其事而結其意也。蓋君子脩身，固本於事親、知人、知天也。然不詳其所以脩身之事而結其意焉，抑何以使人知所從入也哉？《中庸》述孔子荅哀公問政而言及此，意謂為政在人，取人以身，故君子不可以不脩身。脩身以道，脩道以仁，故思脩身不可以
translation_en:
…Some come to understand through study, and some through struggling with difficulties; once they understand, their understanding is the same. Some practice it naturally, some for its benefits, and some through strenuous effort; once they succeed, their achievement is the same. Confucius said: “Loving learning approaches wisdom; putting forth effort in practice approaches benevolence; knowing shame approaches courage. Knowing these three, one knows how to cultivate oneself.”

Yu Wen

Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Assistant Instructor: This is the only essay I have seen that builds its argument around self-cultivation from beginning to end.
Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: An essay on a long topic need not resort to superfluous wording. This composition reduces complexity to simplicity, and its beginning and ending correspond. Here is a true master of composition.
Comment by Associate Examiner Xie, Instructor: The reasoning is clear, and the wording concise and apt. Worth selecting.
Comment by Examiner Xu, Professor: Clear reasoning and fluent prose. Worth selecting.
Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: Although the topic is long, the essay encompasses it without omission. An excellent composition.

The Doctrine of the Mean traces the foundations of the gentleman’s self-cultivation; it must therefore explain its practices fully and draw together their meaning. The gentleman’s self-cultivation is indeed rooted in serving his parents, understanding others, and understanding Heaven. Yet unless the practices by which he cultivates himself are explained fully and their meaning drawn together, how can people be made to know where to begin? The Doctrine of the Mean records Confucius’s reply to Duke Ai’s question about government and proceeds to this point. Its meaning is that governing depends on obtaining the right people, and selecting people depends on one’s own character; therefore, the gentleman must cultivate himself. One cultivates oneself through the Way and cultivates the Way through benevolence. Thus, one who wishes to cultivate himself cannot…

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
不事親欲盡親親之仁必由尊賢之義思事親
可不知人乎親親之殺尊賢之等皆天理也思
知人可不知天乎脩身之本如此而其所以脩
身豈有外於以達德而行達道哉是故天下之
達道五所以行之者三君臣也父子也夫婦也
昆弟也朋友之交也是五者天下古今所共由
之路非達道乎知也仁也勇也是三者天下古
今所同得之理非達德乎達道雖人所共由然
無是三德則無以行之而道非己有矣此行之
===
所以必本乎三德達德雖人所同得然一有不
誠則人欲間之而德非其德矣此行之所以又
本乎一誠然是達道也有生而知之者有學而
知之者有困而知之者其聞道雖有蚤莫及其
知之則同一達道之歸焉有安而行之者有利
而行之者有勉強而行之者其行道雖有難易
及其成功則同一達道之域焉夫以達德而行
達道如此其未及乎達德者可不求以入德之
事乎故好學非知然足以破愚而近乎知力行
punctuated: 不事親。欲盡親親之仁，必由尊賢之義，思事親，可不知人乎？親親之殺、尊賢之等，皆天理也，思知人，可不知天乎？脩身之本如此，而其所以脩身，豈有外於以達德而行達道哉？是故天下之達道五，所以行之者三。君臣也，父子也，夫婦也，昆弟也，朋友之交也，是五者天下古今所共由之路，非達道乎？知也，仁也，勇也，是三者天下古今所同得之理，非達德乎？達道雖人所共由，然無是三德，則無以行之，而道非己有矣。此行之所以必本乎三德。達德雖人所同得，然一有不誠，則人欲間之，而德非其德矣。此行之所以又本乎一誠。然是達道也，有生而知之者，有學而知之者，有困而知之者，其聞道雖有蚤莫，及其知之，則同一達道之歸焉。有安而行之者，有利而行之者，有勉強而行之者，其行道雖有難易，及其成功，則同一達道之域焉。夫以達德而行達道如此，其未及乎達德者，可不求以入德之事乎？故好學非知，然足以破愚而近乎知；力行
translation_en:
…fail to serve his parents. To fulfill the benevolence of loving one’s kin, one must proceed through the righteousness of honoring the worthy. If one wishes to serve one’s parents, can one fail to understand people? The diminishing degrees of affection for kin and the gradations of honor accorded to the worthy are all principles of Heaven. If one wishes to understand people, can one fail to understand Heaven? Such is the foundation of self-cultivation. How could the means of cultivating oneself lie outside practicing the universally binding ways through the universal virtues?

Thus, there are five universally binding ways under Heaven, and three virtues by which they are practiced. Ruler and minister, father and son, husband and wife, elder and younger brothers, and the intercourse of friends: these five are paths followed in common by all under Heaven, past and present. Are they not universally binding ways? Wisdom, benevolence, and courage: these three are principles possessed in common by all under Heaven, past and present. Are they not universal virtues? Although the universally binding ways are followed by everyone, without these three virtues one has no means of practicing them, and the Way is not truly one’s own. This is why their practice must be rooted in the three virtues. Although the universal virtues are possessed by everyone, any lack of sincerity allows human desires to intrude, and virtue ceases to be true virtue. This is why their practice must also be rooted in the single principle of sincerity.

As for these universally binding ways, some know them from birth, some come to know them through study, and some come to know them through difficulty. Although they hear of the Way earlier or later, once they know it, they arrive alike at the same universally binding Way. Some practice it naturally and at ease, some practice it for its benefits, and some practice it through strenuous effort. Although their practice of the Way differs in difficulty or ease, once they achieve success, they reach alike the same realm of the universally binding Way.

Such is the practice of the universally binding ways through the universal virtues. Can those who have not yet attained these virtues fail to seek the practices through which they may enter into virtue? Thus, loving learning is not wisdom, but it suffices to dispel ignorance and bring one close to wisdom; earnest practice…

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
非仁然足以忘私而近乎仁知恥非勇然足以
起懦而近乎勇誠能知此三近則所以入達德
而行達道者在此所以盡事親而知天人者在
此豈不知所以脩身乎盖知所以脩身則取人
有則治人有本而政焉有不舉者哉大抵人君
一身天下國家之本故聖人因哀公問政既告
以人存政舉而又推本於脩身之道如此誠以
人君能脩其身則有君有臣而政之舉也何有
故下文即繼之曰知所以脩身則知所以治人
===
知所以治人則知所以治天下國家矣中庸引
此以繼大舜文武周公之緒豈無意歟
鄉田同井出入相友守望相助疾病相扶持
則百姓親睦方里而井井九百畝其中為
公田八家皆私百畝同養公田
王華
同考試官教諭吳批此作發明井田之善形體之制
殆無遺蘊盖用心於本領之學者也
考試官教授徐批孟子論助法處善於形容足見學識
punctuated:
非仁，然足以忘私而近乎仁；知恥非勇，然足以起懦而近乎勇。誠能知此三近，則所以入達德而行達道者在此，所以盡事親而知天人者在此，豈不知所以脩身乎？盖知所以脩身，則取人有則，治人有本，而政焉有不舉者哉？大抵人君一身，天下國家之本。故聖人因哀公問政，既告以人存政舉，而又推本於脩身之道如此。誠以人君能脩其身，則有君有臣，而政之舉也何有？故下文即繼之曰：「知所以脩身，則知所以治人；知所以治人，則知所以治天下國家矣。」《中庸》引此以繼大舜、文武、周公之緒，豈無意歟？
「鄉田同井，出入相友，守望相助，疾病相扶持，則百姓親睦。方里而井，井九百畝，其中為公田，八家皆私百畝，同養公田。」
王華
同考試官教諭吳批：「此作發明井田之善、形體之制，殆無遺蘊，盖用心於本領之學者也。」
考試官教授徐批：「孟子論助法處，善於形容，足見學識。」
translation_en:
…is not benevolence, yet it suffices to make one forget selfish interests and draw near to benevolence; knowing shame is not courage, yet it suffices to rouse the timid and draw near to courage. If one truly understands these three approaches, herein lies the means to attain the universally applicable virtues and practice the universally applicable Way; herein also lies the means to fulfill one’s service to one’s parents and understand Heaven and humanity. Would one then not know how to cultivate oneself? For if one knows how to cultivate oneself, one has a standard for selecting men and a foundation for governing them. How could government then fail to be carried out? In general, the ruler’s own person is the foundation of all under Heaven, the state, and the family. Thus, when Duke Ai asked about government, the Sage first told him that when the right men are present, government flourishes, and then traced its foundation back to the way of self-cultivation in this manner. Truly, if the ruler can cultivate himself, ruler and ministers will each fulfill their roles; what difficulty could there be in carrying out government? Hence the following text immediately continues: “Knowing how to cultivate oneself, one knows how to govern others; knowing how to govern others, one knows how to govern all under Heaven, the state, and the family.” Could the Doctrine of the Mean have quoted this to carry forward the legacy of the great Shun, Kings Wen and Wu, and the Duke of Zhou without a purpose?

“Those whose village fields share the same well-field befriend one another in going out and returning, assist one another in keeping watch, and support one another in sickness. Thus the common people become affectionate and harmonious. A square measuring one li on each side forms a well-field. Each well-field comprises nine hundred mu, with the public field at its center. Each of eight households has one hundred mu as its private allotment, and together they cultivate the public field.”

Wang Hua.

Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: “This essay elucidates the merits of the well-field system and the arrangements governing its physical layout, leaving scarcely anything unexplored. Its author has evidently devoted himself to learning that addresses the fundamentals.”

Examiner Xu, Professor, comments: “In treating Mencius’s discussion of the system of assisting in cultivation, the essay excels at exposition, amply demonstrating the author’s learning and understanding.”

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授王批說理詳明無踰此篇
大賢告滕臣以井田之善必詳其形體之制也
蓋井田王政之本大賢之於滕臣得不言其善
而復詳其制以告之哉昔孟子因畢戰問井地
上文既告以九一而助矣至此言助法之善若
曰王政莫先於養民養民莫善於助法彼一鄉
之田八家同井出而作也聲應氣求相友而出
入而息也心孚形契相友而入或寇盜之不虞
同謀以防禦之或疾病之不測協力以扶持之
===
是則一鄉之民雖異姓也而於出入守望之間
一恩愛之相結何有於不親乎同井之人雖各
家也而於疾病扶持之際一情義之相維何有
於不睦乎井田之善如此苟不詳其形體之制
抑何使之有所據而行哉是故方里之間畫為
一井一井之地畫為九區一區則為田百畝焉
九區則為田九百畝焉中百畝為公田此公家
所斂以為君子之常祿也外八百畝為私田此
八家所受以為野人之常產也然公田非自養
punctuated:
考試官教授王批：說理詳明，無踰此篇。
大賢告滕臣以井田之善，必詳其形體之制也。蓋井田王政之本，大賢之於滕臣，得不言其善而復詳其制以告之哉？昔孟子因畢戰問井地，上文既告以九一而助矣。至此言助法之善，若曰：王政莫先於養民，養民莫善於助法。彼一鄉之田，八家同井，出而作也，聲應氣求，相友而出；入而息也，心孚形契，相友而入。或寇盜之不虞，同謀以防禦之；或疾病之不測，協力以扶持之。是則一鄉之民，雖異姓也，而於出入守望之間，一恩愛之相結，何有於不親乎？同井之人，雖各家也，而於疾病扶持之際，一情義之相維，何有於不睦乎？井田之善如此，苟不詳其形體之制，抑何使之有所據而行哉？是故方里之間，畫為一井；一井之地，畫為九區。一區則為田百畝焉，九區則為田九百畝焉。中百畝為公田，此公家所斂以為君子之常祿也；外八百畝為私田，此八家所受以為野人之常產也。然公田非自養
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: No essay surpasses this one in the detail and clarity with which it explains the principles.
When the great worthy explained the merits of the well-field system to the minister of Teng, he necessarily set out its physical arrangement in detail.
The well-field system is the foundation of kingly government. In addressing the minister of Teng, how could the great worthy fail to explain its merits and then describe its arrangement in detail? Formerly, when Bi Zhan asked about well-fields, Mencius had already told him, in the preceding passage, to employ the system of communal assistance, with one plot in nine devoted to public cultivation. Here he proceeds to explain the merits of this system, as if to say: In kingly government, nothing takes precedence over nourishing the people; for nourishing the people, nothing is better than the system of communal assistance. On the land of a single village, eight households share one well-field. When they go out to work, they respond to one another’s voices and seek out kindred spirits, going out as companions. When they return to rest, their hearts trust one another and their conduct accords, and they return as companions. Should robbers or bandits appear unexpectedly, they plan together to defend against them; should illness strike without warning, they join forces to support one another.
Thus, although the people of a village bear different surnames, in going out and returning, keeping watch and guarding against danger, they are bound together by shared kindness and affection. How could they fail to be close? Although those sharing a well-field belong to separate households, in supporting one another through illness they are held together by shared feeling and a sense of obligation. How could they fail to live harmoniously? Such are the merits of the well-field system. Yet unless its physical arrangement is explained in detail, how can they have a basis on which to put it into practice? Accordingly, an area one li square is marked out as a single well-field, and the land within it is divided into nine plots. Each plot contains one hundred mu of farmland, and the nine plots contain nine hundred mu. The central hundred mu constitute the public field, whose produce the government collects to provide regular stipends for men in office. The outer eight hundred mu constitute the private fields, which the eight households receive as the permanent holdings of cultivators. Yet the public field does not cultivate itself…

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
也必八家同力以養之而東作方興不敢後焉
公田非自治也必八家通力以治之而西成載
穫不敢緩焉井田形體之制如此此周之助法
所以為善而滕之君臣所以當行也歟大抵為
治不行助法則田賦不均而欲治也難矣助法
一行則君子野人各有定業而上下相安此治
之所以興也孟子當法制廢壞之餘因滕文公
使畢戰問井地乃能因畧以致詳推舊而為新
不屑屑於旣往之迹而能合乎先王之意真可
===
謂命世亞聖之才矣惜乎滕之君臣不能潤澤
而行也噫
易
謙尊而光卑而不可踰君子之終也象曰地
中有山謙君子以裒多益寡稱物平施
李旻
同考試官訓導瞿批此依本義講謙彖象之旨殆盡宜取以冠本房
同考試官學正陳批此題夫子傳謙彖象之意作者多遡流
而不求源惟是篇融會本義織組成文佳士也高薦奚忝
punctuated:
也，必八家同力以養之，而東作方興，不敢後焉。公田非自治也，必八家通力以治之，而西成載穫，不敢緩焉。井田形體之制如此，此周之助法所以為善，而滕之君臣所以當行也歟？大抵為治，不行助法，則田賦不均，而欲治也難矣。助法一行，則君子野人各有定業，而上下相安，此治之所以興也。孟子當法制廢壞之餘，因滕文公使畢戰問井地，乃能因畧以致詳，推舊而為新，不屑屑於旣往之迹，而能合乎先王之意，真可謂命世亞聖之才矣。惜乎滕之君臣不能潤澤而行也！噫！

易

謙，尊而光，卑而不可踰，君子之終也。象曰：「地中有山，謙；君子以裒多益寡，稱物平施。」

李旻

同考試官訓導瞿批：「此依本義講謙彖象之旨殆盡，宜取以冠本房。」

同考試官學正陳批：「此題夫子傳謙彖象之意，作者多遡流而不求源。惟是篇融會本義，織組成文，佳士也！高薦奚忝？」
translation_en:
…it must be tended by the combined efforts of the eight households; when spring cultivation begins, they dare not put it last. Nor does the public field cultivate itself: the eight households must pool their labor to cultivate it, and when the autumn crops are ready for harvesting, they dare not delay. Such is the physical arrangement of the well-field system. Is this not why the Zhou system of labor assistance was good, and why the ruler and ministers of Teng ought to have implemented it? In general, if those who govern do not implement the assistance system, land taxes will be unequal, and achieving good government will be difficult. Once the assistance system is implemented, gentlemen and country people each have settled occupations, and those above and below live together in security. This is how good government flourishes. After laws and institutions had fallen into ruin, Duke Wen of Teng sent Bi Zhan to ask Mencius about the well-field system. Mencius was then able to develop a brief outline into a detailed account and renew the old institutions. He did not fuss over the outward traces of the past, but accorded with the intentions of the former kings. Truly, his was the talent of an age-defining figure, the Second Sage. Alas that the ruler and ministers of Teng could not adapt the system suitably and put it into practice! Ah!

Book of Changes

“Modesty brings honor and radiance to those in exalted positions; those in lowly positions cannot be surpassed. Such is the gentleman’s culmination. The Commentary on the Images says: ‘Within the earth there is a mountain: Modesty. The gentleman accordingly reduces what is excessive and supplements what is deficient, weighing things and distributing them equitably.’”

Li Min

Comment by Associate Examiner Qu, Assistant Instructor: “Following the Original Meaning, this essay expounds almost fully the purport of the Commentaries on the Judgment and the Images for Modesty. It should be selected to head the essays in this examining section.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “This topic concerns the Master’s intentions in his commentaries on the Judgment and the Images for Modesty. Most writers trace the stream upstream without seeking its source. This essay alone thoroughly integrates the Original Meaning and weaves it into a composition. Its author is an excellent scholar! How could recommending him highly be undeserved?”

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授徐批依本義立說得旨
考試官教授王批發明謙德功效之旨殆盡佳作也
彖傳申君子能謙之效象傳示君子體謙之功
夫謙而有終自然之理也君子於此可不盡體
謙之功乎宜彖象二傳各極其旨也昔伏羲畫
謙之卦文王係以君子有終之辭吾夫子彖傳
舉而申之若曰謙者人之至德也人能謙以自
處不恃勞而傲物卑以自牧不耀功而忽人由
是位乎尊也其德愈光而自不可掩是始雖晦
===
而終益光也非君子之終乎居乎卑也其德愈
厚而人莫能過是始雖卑而終益尊也非君子
之終乎君子能謙之效如此不有體謙之功其
能然哉觀諸象傳謂夫謙之為卦貞焉艮也其
象為山悔焉坤也其象為地地中有山以卑蘊
高非謙之象乎君子體之以為人之所行或過
於自高非謙也吾則裒之以損其高則多不偏
於多矣人之所為或溺於自卑非謙也吾則益
之以增其卑則寡不偏於寡矣夫多者裒之非
punctuated:
考試官教授徐批：依本義立說，得旨。

考試官教授王批：發明謙德功效之旨殆盡，佳作也。

彖傳申君子能謙之效，象傳示君子體謙之功。夫謙而有終，自然之理也。君子於此，可不盡體謙之功乎？宜彖象二傳各極其旨也。昔伏羲畫謙之卦，文王係以君子有終之辭。吾夫子彖傳舉而申之，若曰：謙者，人之至德也。人能謙以自處，不恃勞而傲物，卑以自牧，不耀功而忽人，由是位乎尊也，其德愈光，而自不可掩。是始雖晦，而終益光也，非君子之終乎？居乎卑也，其德愈厚，而人莫能過。是始雖卑，而終益尊也，非君子之終乎？君子能謙之效如此，不有體謙之功，其能然哉？觀諸象傳，謂夫謙之為卦，貞焉艮也，其象為山；悔焉坤也，其象為地。地中有山，以卑蘊高，非謙之象乎？君子體之，以為人之所行，或過於自高，非謙也，吾則裒之以損其高，則多不偏於多矣；人之所為，或溺於自卑，非謙也，吾則益之以增其卑，則寡不偏於寡矣。夫多者裒之，非

Examiner Xu, Professor, comments: The argument follows the Original Meaning and grasps its purport.

Examiner Wang, Professor, comments: It elucidates almost exhaustively the meaning of the efforts and effects associated with the virtue of modesty. An excellent composition.

The Commentary on the Judgments expounds the effects of the gentleman’s capacity for modesty; the Commentary on the Images shows the work by which the gentleman embodies modesty. That modesty should bring a good outcome is a principle of the natural order. Can the gentleman therefore fail to exert himself fully in embodying modesty? It is fitting that these two commentaries, on the Judgments and on the Images, should each fully develop their respective meanings.

Long ago, Fuxi drew the hexagram Modesty, and King Wen appended the words, “The gentleman has a good outcome.” Our Master took up and elaborated upon these words in the Commentary on the Judgments, as though saying: Modesty is the highest human virtue. If a person can conduct himself modestly, neither relying on his services to treat others arrogantly nor displaying his achievements to slight others, but instead nurturing himself through humility, then, when he occupies an exalted position, his virtue shines all the more brightly and cannot be concealed. Thus, although initially obscure, he becomes ever more illustrious in the end. Is this not the gentleman’s good outcome? When he occupies a lowly position, his virtue grows all the more substantial, and no one can surpass him. Thus, although initially lowly, he becomes ever more honored in the end. Is this not the gentleman’s good outcome? Such are the effects of the gentleman’s capacity for modesty. Without the work of embodying modesty, could he attain them?

Consider the Commentary on the Images. In the hexagram Modesty, the inner trigram is Gen, whose image is a mountain; the outer trigram is Kun, whose image is the earth. People’s actions may also sink into excessive self-abasement, which is not modesty. title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
矯激也正以稱物之宜俾吾之所施一趣於平
何謙如之寡者益之非矯揉也正以稱事之宜
使吾之所行一適乎均何謙似之吁君子體謙
之功如此此其所以獲有終之效也歟大抵滿
招損謙受益理勢然也故徵諸造化天道虧盈
而益謙地道變盈而流謙徵諸幽明鬼神禍盈
而福謙人道惡盈而好謙大哉謙乎為天道之
所益地道之所流鬼神之所福而況於人乎是
宜有終之效悉萃於能謙者之身也然則未純
===
乎謙者可不自裒多益寡始
夫乾確然示人易矣夫坤隤然示人簡矣爻
也者效此者也象也者像此者也爻象動
乎内吉凶見乎外功業見乎變聖人之情
見乎辭天地之大德曰生聖人之大寶曰
位何以守位曰仁何以聚人曰財理財正
辭禁民為非曰義
徐寬
同考試官訓導瞿 批 此作能主卦爻吉凶造化功業立
punctuated:
矯激也，正以稱物之宜，俾吾之所施一趣於平，何謙如之！寡者益之，非矯揉也，正以稱事之宜，使吾之所行一適乎均，何謙似之！吁！君子體謙之功如此，此其所以獲有終之效也歟！大抵滿招損，謙受益，理勢然也。故徵諸造化，天道虧盈而益謙，地道變盈而流謙；徵諸幽明，鬼神禍盈而福謙，人道惡盈而好謙。大哉謙乎！為天道之所益，地道之所流，鬼神之所福，而況於人乎！是宜有終之效悉萃於能謙者之身也。然則未純乎謙者，可不自裒多益寡始？

夫乾，確然示人易矣；夫坤，隤然示人簡矣。爻也者，效此者也；象也者，像此者也。爻象動乎内，吉凶見乎外，功業見乎變，聖人之情見乎辭。天地之大德曰生，聖人之大寶曰位。何以守位？曰仁。何以聚人？曰財。理財、正辭、禁民為非，曰義。

徐寬

同考試官訓導瞿批：此作能主卦爻吉凶造化功業立
translation_en:
…an excessive corrective; rather, it accords precisely with what things require, so that everything I do tends toward balance. What could better exemplify humility? To augment what is deficient is no forced adjustment; rather, it accords precisely with what affairs require, so that all my conduct attains equilibrium. What could better resemble humility? Ah! Such is the gentleman’s work in embodying humility. Is this not how he achieves the result of bringing matters to a successful conclusion? In general, fullness invites loss, while humility receives benefit: principle and circumstance make this so. Thus, to verify this through the workings of creation, the Way of Heaven diminishes the full and benefits the humble; the Way of Earth alters the full and flows toward the humble. To verify it in the unseen and visible realms, spirits bring calamity upon the full and blessings upon the humble; the way of human beings dislikes the full and favors the humble. Great indeed is humility! It receives benefit from the Way of Heaven, the flow of the Way of Earth, and blessings from the spirits—how much more, then, from human beings! It is fitting that the benefits of a successful conclusion should all accrue to those capable of humility. Should not those whose humility is not yet pure begin by reducing excess and supplementing deficiency?

Qian, in its firmness, shows people ease; Kun, in its yielding compliance, shows people simplicity. The lines emulate these; the images represent these. The lines and images move within, and good and ill fortune appear without. Accomplishments appear through transformations, and the sages’ intentions appear in the statements. The great virtue of Heaven and Earth is called giving life; the great treasure of the sage is called position. By what is position maintained? Benevolence. By what are people gathered together? Wealth. Managing wealth, rectifying statements, and prohibiting the people from wrongdoing are called righteousness.

Xu Kuan.

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
說見理真切行文簡當尤宜錄出
同考試官學正陳批此題作者多不切旨是篇文順理明可嘉
考試官教授徐批文有發揮允宜高薦
考試官教授王批發明卦爻吉凶造化功業得旨
造化示易簡之理卦爻備之而吉凶以顯造化
妙生物之德聖人備之而功業以成蓋易簡之
理生物之德一造化之陰陽也故其所以顯於
占筮著於功業者有如是夫何則乾為純陽確
然至健常示人以易之理坤為純陰隤然至順
===
常示人以簡之理乾坤之理如此備是理者不
在於卦爻乎故凡爻之竒偶所以效此易簡者
也卦之消息所以像此易簡者也方其初筮也
曰爻曰象隱然動於蓍卦之中及其既筮也曰
吉曰凶昭然見於蓍卦之外由是利往利涉功
業之妙也於變之動乎內者見焉趨吉避凶聖
人之情也於辭之見乎外者著焉是則卦爻吉
凶之所以顯者以此至若大哉乾元而資始之
無間此天之大德曰生也至哉坤元而資生之
punctuated:
說，見理真切，行文簡當，尤宜錄出。

同考試官學正陳批：此題作者多不切旨，是篇文順理明，可嘉。

考試官教授徐批：文有發揮，允宜高薦。

考試官教授王批：發明卦爻吉凶、造化功業，得旨。

造化示易簡之理，卦爻備之而吉凶以顯；造化妙生物之德，聖人備之而功業以成。蓋易簡之理、生物之德，一造化之陰陽也，故其所以顯於占筮、著於功業者有如是。夫何則？乾為純陽，確然至健，常示人以易之理；坤為純陰，隤然至順，常示人以簡之理。乾坤之理如此，備是理者不在於卦爻乎？故凡爻之竒偶，所以效此易簡者也；卦之消息，所以像此易簡者也。方其初筮也，曰爻曰象，隱然動於蓍卦之中；及其既筮也，曰吉曰凶，昭然見於蓍卦之外。由是利往利涉，功業之妙也，於變之動乎內者見焉；趨吉避凶，聖人之情也，於辭之見乎外者著焉。是則卦爻吉凶之所以顯者以此。至若大哉乾元，而資始之無間，此天之大德曰生也；至哉坤元，而資生之
translation_en:
…sets forth its argument with a penetrating grasp of principle and concise, fitting prose. It particularly deserves to be selected for inclusion.

Associate Examiner Chen, School Instructor, comments: Most who write on this topic fail to address its purport. This essay’s prose flows well and its reasoning is clear: it deserves praise.

Examiner Xu, Professor, comments: The essay develops its meaning fully and certainly deserves recommendation at a high rank.

Examiner Wang, Professor, comments: It elucidates the auspicious and inauspicious indications of hexagrams and lines, and the achievements of the creative transformations, grasping the purport.

The creative transformations reveal the principles of ease and simplicity; the hexagrams and lines embody these fully, so that auspicious and inauspicious outcomes become manifest. The creative transformations wondrously exercise the virtue of giving life to things; the sage embodies this fully, so that achievements are accomplished. For the principles of ease and simplicity and the virtue of giving life to things are alike the yin and yang of the creative transformations. Thus they become manifest in divination and evident in achievements in this way. Why is this? Qian is pure yang: firm and supremely vigorous, it constantly shows people the principle of ease. Kun is pure yin: yielding and supremely compliant, it constantly shows people the principle of simplicity. Such are the principles of Qian and Kun. Is it not in the hexagrams and lines that these principles are fully embodied? Thus the odd and even configurations of the lines emulate this ease and simplicity, while the waning and waxing of the hexagrams represent this ease and simplicity. When divination first begins, the lines and images move imperceptibly within the yarrow stalks and hexagrams. Once divination is complete, auspicious and inauspicious indications appear clearly outside the stalks and hexagrams. Accordingly, the indications that it is beneficial to go forward or to cross a river express the subtle efficacy of achievements, which becomes visible in the changes moving within. Seeking good fortune and avoiding misfortune express the sage’s intent, which becomes evident in the statements appearing without. This, then, is how the auspicious and inauspicious indications of hexagrams and lines become manifest.

As for the greatness of Qian’s primal power, from which all things ceaselessly derive their beginnings: this is what is meant by saying that Heaven’s great virtue is giving life. As for the consummate excellence of Kun’s primal power, from which all things derive their life …

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
不窮此地之大德曰生也天地之德如此備是
德者不在於聖人乎聖人者出必御皇極之位
而後可為民物之主居九五之尊而後可遂民
物之生非聖人之大寶曰位乎位何以守之曰
人而已盖民惟邦本非眾罔與守邦也人何以
聚之曰財而已盖財為民命非財無以養人也
由是理財正辭俾爭訟之端自息禁民為非使
強橫之風不作何莫非一義為之裁制乎是則
造化功業之所以大者以此嗟夫易書一陰陽
===
也陰陽一造化也其理則顯於卦爻吉凶之占
其德則運於聖人功業之盛吾夫子對舉而互
言之誠有以見易書之大有關乎治化不獨為
卜筮發也世以卜筮小吾易者烏足以知易
書
貳公弘化寅亮天地
來登
同考試官教諭李 批 此題多不知貳公當寅亮天地間有
知者又以弘化之詞混講殊無愜意詞明意盡少類此篇
punctuated:
不窮，此地之大德曰生也。天地之德如此，備是德者不在於聖人乎？聖人者，出必御皇極之位，而後可為民物之主；居九五之尊，而後可遂民物之生。非聖人之大寶曰位乎？位何以守之？曰人而已。盖民惟邦本，非眾罔與守邦也。人何以聚之？曰財而已。盖財為民命，非財無以養人也。由是理財正辭，俾爭訟之端自息；禁民為非，使強橫之風不作。何莫非一義為之裁制乎？是則造化功業之所以大者以此。嗟夫！易書，一陰陽也；陰陽，一造化也。其理則顯於卦爻吉凶之占，其德則運於聖人功業之盛。吾夫子對舉而互言之，誠有以見易書之大有關乎治化，不獨為卜筮發也。世以卜筮小吾易者，烏足以知易書？

貳公弘化，寅亮天地。
來登

同考試官教諭李批：此題多不知貳公當寅亮天地，間有知者，又以弘化之詞混講，殊無愜意。詞明意盡，少類此篇。
translation_en:
…inexhaustible: this is what is meant by saying that the great virtue of Earth is life. Such are the virtues of Heaven and Earth. Is it not the sage who possesses these virtues in full? When the sage comes forth, he must occupy the position of august supremacy before he can become lord of the people and all things; he must hold the exalted place of the fifth, yang line before he can fulfill their lives. Is this not what is meant by saying that the sage’s great treasure is his position? By what does he preserve that position? By people alone. For the people are the foundation of the state; without the multitude, there is no one with whom to defend it. By what does he gather the people? By wealth alone. For wealth sustains the people’s lives; without it, there is no means of nourishing them. Accordingly, he manages wealth and rectifies words, so that the causes of contention and litigation subside of themselves; he prohibits the people from wrongdoing, so that violent and overbearing conduct does not arise. What among these measures is not regulated by the single principle of righteousness? This, then, accounts for the greatness of the achievements of creation and transformation.

Ah! The Book of Changes is entirely yin and yang; yin and yang are entirely creation and transformation. Its principles are manifest in the prognostications of good and ill fortune in the hexagrams and their lines; its virtue operates in the grandeur of the sage’s achievements. Our Master sets these matters alongside one another and discusses them reciprocally, truly showing that the greatness of the Book of Changes bears upon government and moral transformation, and that it was not expounded solely for divination. How could those in the world who belittle our Changes as mere divination be capable of understanding the Book of Changes?

“Assist the Three Dukes in extending transformation, and reverently aid Heaven and Earth.”
By Lai Deng.

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: In treating this topic, most fail to understand that assisting the Three Dukes entails reverently aiding Heaven and Earth. Even the occasional writer who understands this muddles the explanation with the wording about extending transformation, producing a wholly unsatisfactory result. Few essays resemble this one in clarity of expression and fullness of meaning.

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授徐批此題作者多昧贰公之意是篇深契本旨
考試官教授王批理明詞贍非群筆所到
副三公以盡參贊之責此三孤之職也盖三孤
之副三公惟在弘化以寅亮天地也三孤之職
如此其責不亦重乎昔成王訓迪厥官先之三
公而遂及於三孤若曰論道固三公之責也三
孤則貳三公以弘其化焉盖化者天地之妙用
而道則天地之本也使三公論道而非三孤貳
之以弘化則斯道之用或有所未闡萬物何由
===
===
而育哉孤必於化也弘而大之以盡範圍之責
使寒往暑来而為春為夏者各順其序而生生
之妙無窮暑往寒来而為秋為冬者各得其常
而化化之功罔極如是則萬物可育三公所論
之道豈不於是而益闡乎然道化既弘則天地
可得而寅亮矣彼燮理陰陽固三公之任也三
孤則副三公以寅亮天地焉盖天地者陰陽之
實體而陰陽則天地之氣也使三公燮理陰陽
而非三孤副之以寅亮天地則陰陽之和或有
punctuated:
考試官教授徐批：此題作者多昧贰公之意，是篇深契本旨。
考試官教授王批：理明詞贍，非群筆所到。
副三公以盡參贊之責，此三孤之職也。盖三孤之副三公，惟在弘化以寅亮天地也。三孤之職如此，其責不亦重乎？昔成王訓迪厥官，先之三公，而遂及於三孤，若曰：論道固三公之責也，三孤則貳三公以弘其化焉。盖化者天地之妙用，而道則天地之本也。使三公論道，而非三孤貳之以弘化，則斯道之用或有所未闡，萬物何由而育哉？孤必於化也弘而大之，以盡範圍之責，使寒往暑来而為春為夏者各順其序，而生生之妙無窮；暑往寒来而為秋為冬者各得其常，而化化之功罔極。如是，則萬物可育，三公所論之道豈不於是而益闡乎？然道化既弘，則天地可得而寅亮矣。彼燮理陰陽，固三公之任也，三孤則副三公以寅亮天地焉。盖天地者陰陽之實體，而陰陽則天地之氣也。使三公燮理陰陽，而非三孤副之以寅亮天地，則陰陽之和或有

Examiner Xu, Professor, comments: Most who write on this topic fail to understand the meaning of assisting the Three Dukes. This essay accords closely with the original purport.
Examiner Wang, Professor, comments: Clear in reasoning and ample in expression, this is beyond the reach of ordinary writers.
To assist the Three Dukes and fully discharge the responsibility of participating in and aiding the work of transformation: this is the office of the Three Junior Dukes. Their assistance to the Three Dukes consists precisely in extending transforming influence so as reverently to assist Heaven and Earth. Such being their office, is their responsibility not weighty indeed? Formerly, when King Cheng instructed his officials, he began with the Three Dukes and then proceeded to the Three Junior Dukes. It was as though he said: Discussing the Way is indeed the responsibility of the Three Dukes; the Three Junior Dukes assist them in extending its transforming influence. Transformation is the wondrous operation of Heaven and Earth, while the Way is their foundation. If the Three Dukes discussed the Way without the Three Junior Dukes assisting them in extending transformation, some part of the Way’s operation might remain undeveloped. How, then, could the myriad things be nourished?
The Junior Dukes must broaden and enlarge transformation, fully discharging their responsibility to encompass and regulate it. They must ensure that, as cold departs and warmth arrives, spring and summer each follow their proper sequence, so that the wonder of life continually generating life is inexhaustible; and that, as warmth departs and cold arrives, autumn and winter each maintain their proper regularity, so that the achievement of transformation following transformation is boundless. In this way the myriad things can be nourished. Would not the Way discussed by the Three Dukes thereby become still more fully manifest?
Once the Way and its transforming influence have been extended, Heaven and Earth can be reverently assisted. Harmonizing yin and yang is indeed the charge of the Three Dukes; the Three Junior Dukes assist them in reverently aiding Heaven and Earth. Heaven and Earth are the substantial embodiment of yin and yang, while yin and yang are the vital energies of Heaven and Earth. If the Three Dukes harmonized yin and yang without the Three Junior Dukes assisting them in reverently aiding Heaven and Earth, then the harmony of yin and yang might in some respects …

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
所未充天地何由而位哉孤必於天地也敬而
明之以致欽若之心俾日月星辰之麗於上莫
不各安其所而無薄蝕之咎華嶽河海之麗於
下莫不各奠其位而無崩竭之虞如是則天地
可位三公所燮之陰陽豈不於是而益和乎成

他務而汲汲於董正治官蓋以國家紀綱所係
根本所關爲至重也故於此旣重公孤之托而
===
下文又繼之六卿九牧至於凡有官君子莫不
拳拳訓戒無非欲其相與致治於未亂保邦於
