于刑之中率乂于民棐彝
punctuated:
所未充，天地何由而位哉？孤必於天地也敬而明之，以致欽若之心，俾日月星辰之麗於上，莫不各安其所而無薄蝕之咎；華嶽河海之麗於下，莫不各奠其位而無崩竭之虞。如是則天地可位，三公所燮之陰陽，豈不於是而益和乎？成王以是而訓迪三孤，其責望輔己之意深矣！抑考成王當君臨萬邦之日，六服承德之餘，不遑他務，而汲汲於董正治官，蓋以國家紀綱所係、根本所關爲至重也。故於此旣重公孤之托，而下文又繼之六卿九牧，至於凡有官君子，莫不拳拳訓戒，無非欲其相與致治於未亂、保邦於未危也。成王其賢矣哉！

德威惟畏，德明惟明。乃命三后恤功于民：伯夷降典，折民惟刑；禹平水土，主名山川；稷降播種，農殖嘉穀。三后成功，惟殷于民。士制百姓于刑之中，以教祗德。穆穆在上，明明在下，灼于四方，罔不惟德之勤。故乃明于刑之中，率乂于民，棐彝。
translation_en:
…may not be fully realized; how, then, could Heaven and Earth take their proper places? The Three Junior Dukes must reverently assist and illuminate Heaven and Earth, fully expressing a disposition of respectful conformity. Thus the sun, moon, and stars arrayed above will each rest securely in their proper places, without the calamity of eclipses; and the great mountains, rivers, and seas arrayed below will each be firmly established in their positions, without danger of collapse or exhaustion. In this way Heaven and Earth can take their proper places. Would not the yin and yang harmonized by the Three Dukes thereby become still more harmonious? King Cheng instructed and guided the Three Junior Dukes in this manner: profound indeed were his expectations that they should assist him!

Moreover, consider King Cheng when he ruled over the myriad states. Even after the six zones of submission had acknowledged his virtue, he found no leisure for other affairs, but urgently applied himself to supervising and rectifying the officials of government. This was because he regarded matters affecting the state's governing order and foundations as supremely important. Thus, having here emphasized the trust placed in the Three Dukes and Three Junior Dukes, he went on in the ensuing text to address the Six Ministers and Nine Regional Governors. His earnest instructions and admonitions extended to every gentleman holding office. His sole desire was that they should work together to secure good government before disorder arose and preserve the state before danger appeared. How worthy King Cheng was!

“The awe inspired by virtue alone is truly to be feared; the illumination of virtue alone is true illumination. He therefore commanded three lords to devote themselves to meritorious service for the people. Bo Yi promulgated the statutes, restraining the people through penal rules; Yu brought the waters and lands into order and assigned names to the mountains and rivers; Ji taught sowing, cultivating the fine grains. The three lords accomplished their work, richly benefiting the people. The Director of Justice regulated the common people through punishments that struck the proper mean, teaching them to revere virtue. Majestic was the ruler above; enlightened were his ministers below. Their brilliance shone throughout the four quarters, and none failed to exert themselves in virtue. Thus they understood the proper mean in punishment, led the people into good order, and supported the enduring norms.”

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
侯聘
同考試官教諭李批此題頭緒雖多而前後實有関鍵作者多泛講無切是篇獨能發出有虞先德後刑之意関發有此眼不能不為之明也
考試官教授徐批此題前後言刑主意有在是作得之
考試官教授王批發明穆王訓刑之意始盡佳作也
賢王歴叙聖世君臣德業盛而尤用夫刑必申
言其所以用刑之故也盖德者化民之本而刑
特以輔其不及而已聖世君臣所以必先於德
而後用刑者豈非化之不従而刑所不容已耶
===
昔穆王訓刑之意若曰帝舜之世苗以虐為威
也帝反其道以德威而天下無不畏苗以察為
明也帝反其道以德明而天下無不明然聖人
既以德為化民之本乃命三后致憂民之功伯
夷降典以折斯民之邪妄所以正民心也禹平
水土以主有名之山川所以定民居也稷降播
種農殖嘉穀又所以厚民生焉三后各成其功
故民得以殷盛而富庶也民生既厚尤命臯陶
為士師之官制百姓於刑辟之中非以殘民也
punctuated:
侯聘

同考試官教諭李批：此題頭緒雖多，而前後實有関鍵。作者多泛講，無切。是篇獨能發出有虞先德後刑之意，関發有此眼，不能不為之明也。

考試官教授徐批：此題前後言刑，主意有在，是作得之。

考試官教授王批：發明穆王訓刑之意始盡，佳作也。

賢王歴叙聖世君臣德業盛，而尤用夫刑，必申言其所以用刑之故也。盖德者化民之本，而刑特以輔其不及而已。聖世君臣所以必先於德而後用刑者，豈非化之不従，而刑所不容已耶？

昔穆王訓刑之意，若曰：帝舜之世，苗以虐為威也，帝反其道，以德威而天下無不畏；苗以察為明也，帝反其道，以德明而天下無不明。然聖人既以德為化民之本，乃命三后致憂民之功。伯夷降典，以折斯民之邪妄，所以正民心也；禹平水土，以主有名之山川，所以定民居也；稷降播種，農殖嘉穀，又所以厚民生焉。三后各成其功，故民得以殷盛而富庶也。民生既厚，尤命臯陶為士師之官，制百姓於刑辟之中，非以殘民也。
translation_en:
Hou Pin

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: Although this topic has many strands, there is a crucial connection between its earlier and later portions. Most writers discuss it vaguely, without getting to the point. This essay alone brings out the intention of the ruler of Youyu to put virtue first and punishment second. Its exposition possesses this insight [?], which must be brought to light.

Comment by Examiner Xu, Professor: The references to punishment at the beginning and end of this topic have a particular underlying purpose. This composition grasps it.

Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: Only here is King Mu’s intention in his instructions on punishments fully elucidated. An excellent composition.

The worthy king recounts in sequence the flourishing virtue and achievements of ruler and ministers in the age of the sage, yet gives particular attention to their use of punishment. He must therefore explain further why they employed punishment. For virtue is the foundation for transforming the people, while punishment merely supplements what virtue cannot accomplish. Surely the reason why the ruler and ministers of the sage’s age invariably put virtue first and employed punishment afterward was that some would not heed their transforming influence, making punishment unavoidable?

Long ago, the meaning of King Mu’s instructions on punishments was as though he said: In the age of Emperor Shun, the Miao used cruelty to inspire awe. The emperor reversed their approach, inspiring awe through virtue, and none under Heaven failed to stand in awe. The Miao took searching scrutiny for discernment. The emperor reversed their approach, displaying discernment through virtue, and none under Heaven failed to become enlightened. Yet, having established virtue as the foundation for transforming the people, the sage then commanded the three lords to accomplish their work of caring for the people. Boyi promulgated the ordinances to curb the people’s wickedness and waywardness: this was how he rectified their hearts. Yu brought the waters and land into order and took charge of the renowned mountains and rivers: this was how he secured the people’s dwellings. Ji instructed them in sowing and planting, cultivating fine grains: this, in turn, was how he enriched their livelihoods. Each of the three lords accomplished his work, and thus the people were able to flourish, becoming prosperous and numerous. Once their livelihoods had been enriched, the emperor further appointed Gao Yao as Judge, keeping the common people within the bounds of penal law. This was not intended to injure the people …

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
所以檢其心而教以敬德焉非以虐民也所以
治其心而導以祇德焉然聖人所以必先德而
後刑者何哉盖以刑非所恃為治不得已而用
之耳觀之當時在上而為君者德威德明穆穆
而有和敬之容在下而為臣者恤民殷民明明
而有精白之容一穆穆之德昭灼於四方一明
明之德敷著於天下故民之得於觀感者莫不
惟德之是勤囿于甄陶者靡不惟德之是敏如
是而尤有未化者刑其可已乎故士師明于五
===
刑之中使無過不及之差輕重各得其宜取舎
咸當其可率乂于民輔其常性于以去其舊染
之汙于以復其本然之善則所以教祗德者寧
不在是乎穆王以是而訓刑可謂得有虞用刑
之意矣抑考吕刑一書雖原訓刑而作然刑之
本必主於德刑之用必合乎中故穆王訓刑以
誥四方厯叙聖世德化之本末而歸之於臯陶
明刑之中繼此曰惟克天德曰以成三德無非
以德為本也曰觀于五刑之中曰中聽獄之兩
punctuated:
所以檢其心而教以敬德焉，非以虐民也，所以治其心而導以祇德焉。然聖人所以必先德而後刑者，何哉？盖以刑非所恃為治，不得已而用之耳。觀之當時，在上而為君者，德威德明，穆穆而有和敬之容；在下而為臣者，恤民殷民，明明而有精白之容。一穆穆之德昭灼於四方，一明明之德敷著於天下，故民之得於觀感者，莫不惟德之是勤；囿于甄陶者，靡不惟德之是敏。如是而尤有未化者，刑其可已乎？故士師明于五刑之中，使無過不及之差，輕重各得其宜，取舎咸當其可，率乂于民，輔其常性，于以去其舊染之汙，于以復其本然之善，則所以教祗德者，寧不在是乎？穆王以是而訓刑，可謂得有虞用刑之意矣。
抑考《吕刑》一書，雖原訓刑而作，然刑之本必主於德，刑之用必合乎中。故穆王訓刑，以誥四方，厯叙聖世德化之本末，而歸之於臯陶明刑之中。繼此曰「惟克天德」，曰「以成三德」，無非以德為本也。曰「觀于五刑之中」，曰「中聽獄之兩
translation_en:
…it was to restrain their hearts and teach them to revere virtue. It was not to oppress the people, but to put their hearts in order and guide them to honor virtue. Yet why must the sage invariably put virtue first and punishment afterward? Because punishment is not what one relies upon to govern; it is used only when unavoidable. Looking at that time, the ruler above inspired awe through virtue and brought enlightenment through virtue, dignified in bearing and displaying harmony and reverence. The ministers below cared for the people and made them prosperous, radiant in bearing and displaying purity and integrity. The dignified virtue of the one shone throughout the four quarters; the radiant virtue of the others spread throughout the realm. Thus, among the people moved by observing their example, none failed to apply themselves diligently to virtue; among those encompassed by their molding influence, none failed to pursue virtue assiduously. If even then some remained untransformed, could punishment be dispensed with? Hence the Chief Criminal Judge discerned the proper measure in the five punishments, allowing neither excess nor deficiency. Lighter and heavier penalties each received their appropriate application, and decisions to impose or forgo them were all fitting. He led the people into good order and sustained their enduring moral nature, thereby removing the stains of their former corrupting influences and restoring their original goodness. Surely this was precisely how they were taught to honor virtue? In issuing instructions on punishment on this basis, King Mu may be said to have grasped the intent with which the ruler of Youyu, Shun, employed punishment.
Moreover, when we examine the text of the Punishments of Lü, although it was originally composed to give instruction concerning punishment, punishment must be grounded in virtue, and its application must accord with the proper measure. Thus, when King Mu instructed the four quarters concerning punishment, he recounted in sequence the foundations and unfolding of moral transformation in the age of the sages, culminating in Gao Yao’s discerning application of the proper measure in punishment. The ensuing statements, “Only by being capable of Heaven’s virtue” and “Thereby to bring the three virtues to completion,” both take virtue as their foundation. It says, “Examine the proper measure in the five punishments,” and “With impartiality, hear the two …

text:
辭無非以中為用也要之刑必合中而後刑即
所以為德穆王訓刑而拳拳及此此其所以為
可取歟
詩
天保定爾亦孔之固俾爾單厚何福不除俾
爾多益以莫不庶天保定爾俾爾戩穀罄
無不宜受天百祿降爾遐福維日不足天
保定爾以莫不興如山如阜如岡如陵如
川之方至以莫不增
===
俞前穩

考試官教授徐批此作深合傳意

辭，無非以中為用也。要之，刑必合中，而後刑即所以為德。穆王訓刑而拳拳及此，此其所以為可取歟？

詩

translation_en:
…statements—all these take due balance as the principle governing the application of punishment. In sum, punishment must accord with due balance before it can itself serve to realize virtue. King Mu, in his instructions on punishment, repeatedly and earnestly addressed this point. Is this not what makes those instructions worthy of approval?

Book of Odes

Heaven protects and establishes you, with great firmness indeed. It makes your blessings abundant and substantial: what blessing does it not bestow? It grants you increase upon increase, so that nothing fails to abound. Heaven protects and establishes you, granting you happiness and goodness. Everything is fitting, without exception; you receive Heaven’s hundred blessings. It sends down enduring blessings upon you, as though each day were insufficient. Heaven protects and establishes you, so that nothing fails to flourish. Like mountains and hills, like ridges and heights, like a river’s swelling current, nothing fails to increase.

Yu Qianwen 俞前穩

Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Assistant Instructor: This topic comprises three stanzas. Writers often fail to distinguish their divisions clearly and make very serious errors. This essay alone develops the meaning of subjects responding to their ruler. It is included here to dispel the many doubts.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: Composed in a single sustained flow, it preserves the meaning of the commentary. Could those presiding over the examination fail to regard its author with fresh respect?

Comment by Associate Examiner Xie, Instructor: It expresses subjects’ loyalty and love toward their ruler, a warmth that overflows beyond the words themselves. For this reason it is included.

Comment by Examiner Xu, Professor: This composition accords closely with the meaning of the commentary.

Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: Both expression and reasoning are fully accomplished. It merits selection.

A subject repeatedly invokes Heaven to bless his ruler, not only describing in detail the abundance of his blessings, but also drawing comparisons…

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
其福之盛蓋臣受君賜舍祝福無以為報也使
徒詳言其福而不擬物以形容之何以見其祝
君之至哉昔天保臣子荅君之賜而祝其福若
曰君之備禮以燕臣下也至矣我將何以為報
乎惟願天於冥冥之中所以安定我君者為甚
固焉則使我君之福日積月累以至於單厚但
見往者盡而來者繼何福之不除舊生新乎使
我君之福日新月盛以至於多益但見來如幾
而多如式何福之不既庶且繁乎祝君至此若
===
已至矣又願天於蒼蒼之表所以安定我君者
為益隆焉則使我君每事盡善無適而不攸宜
者既受百禄於天矣天又申以無窮之福維日
不足焉每事皆嘉無往而不自適者既膺多福
於天矣天又錫以無疆之休維日不已焉祝君
至此若已足矣又願上天安定我君使是單厚
也多益也由此而益興百禄也遐福也於茲而
益盛擬之以地勢則如山阜岡陵高大而不可
測其增也何如擬之以水勢則如川流方至盛
punctuated: 其福之盛。蓋臣受君賜，舍祝福無以為報也。使徒詳言其福，而不擬物以形容之，何以見其祝君之至哉？昔《天保》，臣子荅君之賜而祝其福，若曰：「君之備禮以燕臣下也至矣，我將何以為報乎？惟願天於冥冥之中，所以安定我君者為甚固焉，則使我君之福日積月累，以至於單厚，但見往者盡而來者繼，何福之不除舊生新乎？使我君之福日新月盛，以至於多益，但見來如幾而多如式，何福之不既庶且繁乎？祝君至此，若已至矣。又願天於蒼蒼之表，所以安定我君者為益隆焉，則使我君每事盡善，無適而不攸宜者，既受百禄於天矣，天又申以無窮之福，維日不足焉；每事皆嘉，無往而不自適者，既膺多福於天矣，天又錫以無疆之休，維日不已焉。祝君至此，若已足矣。又願上天安定我君，使是單厚也、多益也，由此而益興；百禄也、遐福也，於茲而益盛。擬之以地勢，則如山阜岡陵，高大而不可測，其增也何如？擬之以水勢，則如川流方至，盛
translation_en:
…the abundance of his blessings. For when a minister receives gifts from his ruler, he has no way to repay them except by praying for blessings upon him. If he merely described those blessings in detail, without comparing them to things to give them visible form, how could he show the utmost sincerity of his prayers for his ruler? In the past, in “Heaven Protects” (Tian bao), ministers responded to their ruler’s gifts by praying for blessings upon him, as though saying:

“Our ruler has shown the greatest care in providing the proper rites for feasting his ministers. How shall we repay him? We wish only that Heaven, in its unseen workings, will make the means by which it secures our ruler exceedingly firm. Then our ruler’s blessings will accumulate day after day and month after month, until they become substantial and abundant. We shall see only that, as earlier blessings are exhausted, new ones follow. What blessing will fail to shed the old and bring forth the new? May our ruler’s blessings grow fresh each day and flourish each month, until they become ever more numerous. We shall see them arrive as expected and multiply according to their proper measure [?]. What blessing will fail to be plentiful and profuse? Prayers for our ruler that reach this point might seem already to have reached their utmost extent.

“Yet we further wish that Heaven, beyond the blue vault, will make the means by which it secures our ruler still more ample. Then our ruler, perfect in every undertaking and acting fittingly wherever he turns, will already have received Heaven’s hundred blessings; yet Heaven will add inexhaustible blessings, as though the days were insufficient for bestowing them. Excellent in every undertaking and at ease wherever he goes, he will already have received Heaven’s many blessings; yet Heaven will further grant boundless favor, never ceasing from day to day. Prayers for our ruler that reach this point might seem already sufficient.

“Yet we further wish that Heaven above will secure our ruler, causing this abundance and these multiplying benefits to grow still greater, and these hundred blessings and enduring blessings to flourish still more. Compared to the forms of the land, they are like mountains, hills, ridges, and heights, so lofty and vast that they cannot be measured: how great their increase! Compared to the movement of water, they are like a river’s current newly arriving, swelling…”

長而不可量其增也何若吁人臣祝君之福稱
述之既詳而形容之尤切忠愛之意何其至歟

荅之拳拳祝頌有加而無已所謂上以是施之

…growing beyond measure: how great would that increase be? Ah! In invoking blessings upon their ruler, his servants describe them fully and portray them with particular aptness. How profound is their loyal affection! Broadly speaking, all six stanzas of this ode are the words of subjects responding to their ruler. Looking back at the preceding odes, the ruler uses “The Deer Call” (Lu ming) to feast honored guests, “The Four Stallions” (Si mu) and “The Glorious Flowers” (Huang hua) to feast emissaries, and “The Cherry Tree” (Chang di) and “Felling Trees” (Fa mu) to feast brothers and friends. His gracious concern for those below may indeed be called abundant. His subjects therefore respond with heartfelt blessings and praise, ever increasing and never ceasing. This is what is meant by those above bestowing such favors and those below repaying them in kind. Considered together, these odes enable us to imagine the harmonious relations between an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers in that age.
Sharp are the fine plowshares; they begin work in the southern fields. They sow the hundred grains; the seeds swell and come to life. Someone comes to visit you, carrying square and round baskets. The food brought is millet. Your hats are woven of twisted straw; your hoes cut keenly, to weed out bitter herbs and smartweed. The bitter herbs and smartweed decay; the millets flourish. They harvest them in great armfuls and pile them up in masses, high as walls and close-packed as the teeth of a comb, to open and fill the hundred granaries. The hundred granaries are full; wives and children are at peace. They slaughter this yellow bull with black lips, its horns long and curved, to carry on and continue—to continue the work of the men of old.
Wang Yue.

周人力農事而享豐年之樂必脩祀事以紹先
世之傳盖農事有成祀事所由脩也周人既力
農事以樂乎豐年安得不脩祀事以繼其先祖
哉昔周人之務農也當夫東作之時以彼嚴利
之耜而始事南畝之間其耕之也勤矣播此百
穀於南畝而其實含氣以生其種之也時矣言
其餉田婦子則持筐筥之器盛伊黍之具以饟
農夫無珎味也言其耘田農夫則戴輕舉之笠
操刺土之鎛以薅荼蓼無怠力也荼蓼既朽嘉
穀自茂我黍於焉而與與我稷於焉而翼翼苗
盛如此迨夫西成之日穫之於野而桎桎其聲
積之在場而栗栗其密曾謂我田不既臧乎積
之密也而其狀如櫛曾
之高也而其勢如墉積
謂我田不有秋乎百室向也通力合作今則同

…at the points where they connect what precedes with what follows, their writing is fragmented and disjointed. This composition is clear and incisive in conception, vigorous and coherent in expression. Its author surely possesses genuine insight. What is surprising about recommending him so highly?

Associate Examiner Xie, Instructor, comments: “In expounding the meaning of a hymn, concision and antique simplicity are prized. This composition achieves them.”

Examiner Xu, Professor, comments: “Concise and fluent; worthy of acceptance.”

Examiner Wang, Professor, comments: “It brings out the importance the people of Zhou attached to agriculture. Commendable.”

The people of Zhou labored at agriculture and enjoyed the happiness of an abundant year. They necessarily performed the sacrifices to carry on the traditions of earlier generations, for success in agriculture provided the means to perform the sacrifices. Having labored at agriculture and rejoiced in an abundant year, how could the people of Zhou fail to perform the sacrifices and thus continue the practices of their ancestors?

When the people of Zhou formerly devoted themselves to farming, at the season of spring cultivation they took their sharp plowshares and began work in the southern fields. Diligent indeed was their plowing! They sowed the various grains in the southern fields, and the seeds absorbed the vital breath and sprouted. Timely indeed was their sowing! As for the wives and children who brought food to the fields, they carried square and round baskets filled with millet to feed the farmers; there were no rare delicacies. As for the farmers weeding the fields, they wore light bamboo hats and wielded hoes that pierced the earth, rooting out the bitter weeds and smartweed; they spared no effort. Once these weeds had rotted away, the fine grain naturally flourished. Our millet grew luxuriantly, and our other millet stood in orderly ranks: such was the abundance of the shoots.

When the autumn harvest arrived, they reaped in the fields with a clattering sound [?], and stacked the grain densely on the threshing ground. Could anyone say that our fields were not good? Packed closely, the stacks resembled the teeth of a comb; piled high, they rose like walls. Could anyone say that our fields yielded no harvest? title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
時入穀而百室以開矣婦子向也饁彼南畝今
則百室既盈而婦子以寧矣夫農事有成祭祀
之禮容可緩乎於是殺時犉牡而其色也純有
抹其角而其角也曲備此禮物豈徒然哉蓋以
我祖於農事有成之日固嘗行報本之典矣今
則是烝是享于宗廟之神以繼此典於不替焉
我祖於農事甫畢之秋固嘗舉追遠之禮矣今
則以享以祀于宗廟之主以續此禮於不忘焉
吁力農事而利獲於今舉祀事而禮傳於古有
===
周盛時之氣象蓋如是夫載考周家以農事開
國以忠厚養民若后稷之教稼穡公劉之篤民
事文王之即田功武王之重民食皆此意也故
其見於詩風有七月雅有大田頌有載芟良耜
風化之所由來者遠矣八百年靈長之祚豈偶
然哉
春秋
春王正月〔隱公元年〕子同生〔桓公六年〕紀季姜歸
于京師〔桓公九年〕鄭伯使其弟語來盟〔桓公十□□〕
punctuated:
時入穀，而百室以開矣。婦子向也饁彼南畝，今則百室既盈，而婦子以寧矣。夫農事有成，祭祀之禮容可緩乎？於是殺時犉牡，而其色也純；有抹其角，而其角也曲。備此禮物，豈徒然哉？蓋以我祖於農事有成之日，固嘗行報本之典矣。今則是烝是享于宗廟之神，以繼此典於不替焉。我祖於農事甫畢之秋，固嘗舉追遠之禮矣。今則以享以祀于宗廟之主，以續此禮於不忘焉。吁！力農事而利獲於今，舉祀事而禮傳於古，有周盛時之氣象，蓋如是夫！載考周家，以農事開國，以忠厚養民。若后稷之教稼穡，公劉之篤民事，文王之即田功，武王之重民食，皆此意也。故其見於詩，風有《七月》，雅有《大田》，頌有《載芟》《良耜》。風化之所由來者遠矣，八百年靈長之祚，豈偶然哉？

春秋

春，王正月。〔隱公元年〕子同生。〔桓公六年〕紀季姜歸于京師。〔桓公九年〕鄭伯使其弟語來盟。〔桓公十□□〕
translation_en:
…bring in their grain at the same time, and the hundred households open their storehouses. Formerly the wives and children brought food to those southern fields; now the hundred households are full, and the wives and children are at peace. When farming has yielded its harvest, can the rites of sacrifice possibly be delayed? Thus they slaughter that black-lipped yellow bull, its coat uniform in color; its horns are curved [?]. Can the provision of these ritual offerings be without purpose? For our ancestors, when their agricultural labors had borne fruit, certainly performed the ceremony of requiting their origins. Now we present these winter sacrifices and offerings to the spirits of the ancestral temple, continuing this ceremony without allowing it to lapse. Our ancestors, in autumn when agricultural work had just been completed, certainly performed the rites of honoring their distant forebears. Now we make offerings and sacrifices to the ancestral tablets in the temple, perpetuating these rites without forgetting them. Ah! To labor at farming and reap its benefits in the present, and to perform sacrifices according to rites handed down from antiquity—such indeed was the flourishing age of Zhou!

Further examining the house of Zhou, we find that it founded its state through agriculture and nurtured its people through sincerity and generosity. Hou Ji’s teaching of sowing and reaping, Gong Liu’s devotion to the people’s affairs, King Wen’s engagement in agricultural work, and King Wu’s concern for the people’s food all embodied this intention. Thus, in the Book of Odes, the Airs include “The Seventh Month,” the Elegantiae include “The Great Field,” and the Hymns include “Clearing the Grass” and “The Good Ploughshare.” The sources of its moral influence reach far back indeed. Could its enduring dynastic blessing of eight hundred years have been mere chance?

Spring and Autumn Annals

“Spring, the first month of the royal calendar.” 〔First year of Duke Yin.〕
“The son, Tong, was born.” 〔Sixth year of Duke Huan.〕
“Ji Jiang of Ji went to the royal capital to be married.” 〔Ninth year of Duke Huan.〕

The Spring and Autumn Annals sets in order the precedence of human relationships, thereby strengthening the five constant norms; it regulates the distinctions between superior and inferior, thereby putting the five rites into practice. From this we can see that, in composing the Spring and Autumn Annals, the Sage intended to order the world, while his achievement would benefit later ages. Alas! The Way of Zhou had declined, and the constant norms and rites had fallen into disuse and ruin. If the Sage, in whom heavenly principle resided, did not take this as his own responsibility, who could? Thus he drew upon the historical records of Lu to compile the Spring and Autumn Annals, considering that, since the five constant norms were not firmly upheld, it fell to him to set them in order. title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
盟魯而書名罪其有寵愛之私而非友于之義
所以叙夫婦兄弟之倫也魯邾尋蔑之盟而平
再伐之怨則書盟趡而責其無久要之信非所
以叙朋友之倫乎聖人之叙先後之倫如此則
五典由是而可惇矣若夫五禮弗庸己所當秩
也書魯僖之四卜郊以著其非禮僭分而拂人
道之大經書榮叔歸含且賵以見其恩數稠疊
而妄加於諸侯之妾母所以明吉禮凶禮之分
也文公慢王而事伯則書敖之如晉以示譏秦
===
人專兵以虐小則書入鄀之後以寓意所以明
賓禮軍禮之分也書宣公遣卿逆女以責其斬
焉在疚而亟於結昏非所以明嘉禮之分乎聖
人之秩上下之分如此則五禮由是而可庸矣
吁天叙有典非聖人叙之而弗惇天秩有禮非
聖人秩之而弗庸孰謂惇典庸禮有不賴於聖
人乎不特此也他如有德者必褒而五服以章
有罪者必貶而五刑以用其志存乎經世其功
配於抑洪水膺戎狄放龍蛇驅虎豹其大要則
punctuated:
盟魯而書名，罪其有寵愛之私而非友于之義，所以叙夫婦兄弟之倫也。魯邾尋蔑之盟，而平再伐之怨，則書盟趡，而責其無久要之信，非所以叙朋友之倫乎？聖人之叙先後之倫如此，則五典由是而可惇矣。若夫五禮弗庸，己所當秩也。書魯僖之四卜郊，以著其非禮僭分而拂人道之大經；書榮叔歸含且賵，以見其恩數稠疊而妄加於諸侯之妾母，所以明吉禮凶禮之分也。文公慢王而事伯，則書敖之如晉以示譏；秦人專兵以虐小，則書入鄀之後以寓意，所以明賓禮軍禮之分也。書宣公遣卿逆女，以責其斬焉在疚而亟於結昏，非所以明嘉禮之分乎？聖人之秩上下之分如此，則五禮由是而可庸矣。

translation_en:
…when he covenanted with Lu, his personal name was recorded, condemning the partiality of doting affection as contrary to the duty of brotherly love. These are ways of setting in order the relationships between husband and wife and between brothers. Lu and Zhu renewed the covenant of Mie and settled the grievances arising from two attacks; yet the covenant at Cui was recorded to reproach their failure to keep faith with an enduring pledge. Was this not a way of setting in order the relationship between friends? Such was the sage’s ordering of relationships of precedence; through this, the five cardinal duties could be earnestly observed.
As for the failure to practice the five categories of rites, he regarded their ordering as his own responsibility. He recorded Duke Xi of Lu’s four divinations concerning the suburban sacrifice to expose a breach of ritual and a usurpation of status that violated the great norms of human relationships. He recorded Rong Shu’s delivery of both articles to be placed in the deceased’s mouth and gifts for the funeral procession, showing how marks of favor were excessively heaped upon the mother of a feudal lord who had been a concubine. These are ways of clarifying the distinctions governing auspicious and mourning rites. Duke Wen slighted the king while serving the hegemon, so the sage recorded Ao’s journey to Jin to express censure. The people of Qin used military force on their own authority to oppress a small state, so he conveyed his meaning by placing the record of their invasion of Ruo afterward [?]. These are ways of clarifying the distinctions governing rites for receiving guests and military rites. He recorded Duke Xuan’s dispatch of a minister to fetch his bride, reproaching him for hastening to contract a marriage while still grieving in deepest mourning. Was this not a way of clarifying the distinctions governing celebratory rites? Such was the sage’s ordering of distinctions between superior and inferior; through this, the five categories of rites could be practiced.
Ah! Heaven establishes an order with its constant duties, but without the sage to order them, they would not be earnestly observed. Heaven establishes ranks with their rites, but without the sage to arrange them, they would not be practiced. Who could say that earnest observance of these duties and the practice of these rites do not depend upon the sage? Nor is this all. Those possessing virtue must be praised, and thus the robes of the five ranks serve to distinguish them; those guilty of wrongdoing must be censured, and thus the five punishments are applied. His purpose lay in bringing order to the world, and his achievement matched the checking of the floodwaters, the repelling of the Rong and Di, the banishment of dragons and snakes, and the driving away of tigers and leopards. 同考試官訓導韓批〔聖人行道作者類能言之而於明
道處多為所窘認題親切措詞簡當僅見此篇〕
考試官教授徐批〔能明聖人行藏之道可取〕
===
考試官教授王批〔得属詞比事之旨〕
聖人之進也行道以化人而其退也明道以淑
人此孔子行道見於仲由墮邑之時而其明道
則見於冉有勝齊之後也慨夫三家專魯各固
其城遂致陪臣亦專國命而公室之削弱也滋
甚尚何望其負固之都自毀哉幸而仲由為季
氏宰將墮三都時孔子為魯司冦行乎季孫三
月不違諭以家不藏甲邑無百雉之城於是叔
孫首倡帥師而墮郈季孫接武帥師而墮費焉
punctuated:
皆天子之事也。故曰：「知我者，其惟春秋乎！罪我者，其惟春秋乎！」

叔孫州仇帥師墮郈〔定公十二年〕。季孫斯、仲孫何忌帥師墮費〔同上〕。齊國書帥師伐我〔哀公十一年〕。

夏賚

同考試官訓導韓批〔聖人行道，作者類能言之，而於明道處多為所窘。認題親切，措詞簡當，僅見此篇。〕

考試官教授徐批〔能明聖人行藏之道，可取。〕

考試官教授王批〔得属詞比事之旨。〕

聖人之進也，行道以化人；而其退也，明道以淑人。此孔子行道見於仲由墮邑之時，而其明道則見於冉有勝齊之後也。慨夫三家專魯，各固其城，遂致陪臣亦專國命，而公室之削弱也滋甚，尚何望其負固之都自毀哉！幸而仲由為季氏宰，將墮三都。時孔子為魯司冦，行乎季孫，三月不違，諭以家不藏甲、邑無百雉之城。於是叔孫首倡，帥師而墮郈；季孫接武，帥師而墮費焉。
translation_en:
…all are the affairs of the Son of Heaven. Thus he said: “Those who understand me will surely do so through the Spring and Autumn Annals! Those who condemn me will surely do so through the Spring and Autumn Annals!”

“Shusun Zhouchou led an army to demolish the fortifications of Hou.” 〔Twelfth year of Duke Ding.〕 “Jisun Si and Zhongsun Heji led an army to demolish the fortifications of Fei.” 〔Same as above.〕 “Guo Shu of Qi led an army to attack us.” 〔Eleventh year of Duke Ai.〕

Xia Lai

Comment by Associate Examiner Han, Assistant Instructor: 〔Writers generally can discuss the sage’s putting the Way into practice, but most find themselves at a loss when addressing his elucidation of the Way. This essay alone grasps the topic closely and expresses itself concisely and aptly.〕

Comment by Examiner Xu, Instructor: 〔It successfully elucidates the Way underlying the sage’s service and withdrawal, and merits acceptance.〕

Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: 〔It grasps the purpose of arranging words and juxtaposing events.〕

When the sage enters public service, he puts the Way into practice to transform others; when he withdraws, he elucidates the Way to better them. Thus Confucius’s putting the Way into practice is seen when Zhong You demolished the fortified towns, while his elucidation of the Way is seen after Ran You defeated Qi. Alas, the three families monopolized power in Lu, each strengthening its own fortified town. This brought matters to the point where even their retainers monopolized the government of the state, while the ducal house grew ever weaker. What hope could there have been that their towns, relying on strong defenses, would demolish their own fortifications? Fortunately, Zhong You became steward to the Ji family and was about to demolish the fortifications of the three towns. At that time Confucius was Minister of Justice in Lu. His Way prevailed with Jisun, who for three months did not depart from it [?]. He instructed him that great-officer households should not store armor and that their towns should not have walls measuring a hundred zhi. Thereupon Shusun took the lead, commanding troops to demolish the fortifications of Hou; Jisun followed in his footsteps, commanding troops to demolish those of Fei.…

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
仲由之毁盖孔子之意也然郈邑既墮而強榦
弱枝之勢復振費都復毁而以身使臂之義猶
存所謂苟有用我者朞月而已可也為足徴矣
非行道以化人而何若夫齊為郕故師出淄澠
及清涉泗游薄國都而我魯之危殆也亦甚尚
何望其逞憤之兵自退哉幸而冉有用事於魯
運籌却齊欲禦諸境而季孫不能欲居封疆而
二子不可遂自用矛於齊師而致齊人之宵遁
康子因其勝齊有功追季桓子之遺言乃召孔
===
子焉孔子之召由冉有之捷也然孔子知魯終
不能用於是叙書而定禮樂以斯道為已任刪
詩而賛周易翕弟子之景從所謂自衛反魯樂
正雅頌各得其所不徒言也非明道以淑人而
何雖然行道固有功於當時而明道尤有功於
後世有功於當時者一時之幸也有功於後世
者萬世之幸也彼或以聖人之心不得直遂於
當時為足惜而以郈費之墮為後世之美談烏
足以知聖人者哉
punctuated:
仲由之毁，盖孔子之意也。然郈邑既墮，而強榦弱枝之勢復振；費都復毁，而以身使臂之義猶存。所謂「苟有用我者，朞月而已可也」，為足徴矣。非行道以化人而何？若夫齊為郕故，師出淄澠，及清，涉泗游，薄國都，而我魯之危殆也亦甚，尚何望其逞憤之兵自退哉？幸而冉有用事於魯，運籌却齊，欲禦諸境而季孫不能，欲居封疆而二子不可，遂自用矛於齊師，而致齊人之宵遁。康子因其勝齊有功，追季桓子之遺言，乃召孔子焉。

孔子之召，由冉有之捷也。然孔子知魯終不能用，於是叙書而定禮樂，以斯道為已任；刪詩而賛周易，翕弟子之景從。所謂「自衛反魯，樂正，雅頌各得其所」，不徒言也。非明道以淑人而何？雖然，行道固有功於當時，而明道尤有功於後世。有功於當時者，一時之幸也；有功於後世者，萬世之幸也。彼或以聖人之心不得直遂於當時為足惜，而以郈費之墮為後世之美談，烏足以知聖人者哉？
translation_en:
Zhong You’s demolition of the walls was surely Confucius’s intention. Once the walls of Hou had been pulled down, the balance of power that strengthened the trunk and weakened the branches was restored; when the walls of Bi were also demolished, the principle of the body directing its arms remained intact. This amply bears out the saying, “If someone would employ me, twelve months would suffice.” What was this if not putting the Way into practice to transform others? As for Qi, on account of Cheng its army marched out from the Zi and Sheng rivers, reached the Qing River, crossed the Si River [?], and pressed upon the capital. Our state of Lu was in grave peril. How could one still hope that troops bent on venting their anger would withdraw of their own accord? Fortunately, Ran You held responsibility in Lu and devised plans to repel Qi. He wished to resist them at the border, but Jisun was unable to do so; he wished to take up a position on the frontier, but the two gentlemen would not agree. He therefore personally wielded a spear against Qi’s army, causing the men of Qi to flee by night. In view of his achievement in defeating Qi, Ji Kangzi recalled Ji Huanzi’s dying words and summoned Confucius.

Confucius’s recall thus resulted from Ran You’s victory. Yet Confucius knew that Lu would ultimately be unable to employ him. He therefore arranged the Documents and established rites and music, taking responsibility for this Way upon himself. He edited the Odes and elucidated the Changes of Zhou, drawing his disciples together to follow him like shadows. The saying, “After I returned from Wei to Lu, music was set right, and the Court Hymns and Eulogies each found their proper place,” was no empty claim. What was this if not clarifying the Way to make others good? Nevertheless, although putting the Way into practice certainly benefited his own time, clarifying it benefited later generations still more. Benefit to his own time was good fortune for one age; benefit to later generations was good fortune for ten thousand ages. Some may consider it regrettable that the sage could not directly fulfill his aspirations in his own time, and regard the demolition of Hou and Bi as a fine tale for posterity. How could such people be qualified to understand the sage?

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
禮記
有虞氏之祭也尚用氣血腥爓祭用氣也殷
人尚聲臭味未成滌蕩其聲樂三闋然後
出迎牲聲音之號所以詔告於天地之間
也周人尚臭灌用鬯臭鬱合鬯臭陰達於
淵泉灌以圭璋用玉氣也既灌然後迎牲
致陰氣也蕭合黍稷臭陽達於墻屋故既
奠然後焫蕭合羶薌凡祭慎諸此
王華
===
同考試官教諭吳批此題頭緒頗多作者類多冗泛其凡祭慎諸此一句或言單者或言群祀殊無定見此篇理明詞順尤宜高薦
考試官教授徐批見理明行文暢是用錄出
考試官教授王批說出歷代廟祭之禮可取
知歷代之致祭各有所尚當知歷代之致祭各
謹所尚盖虞尚氣殷尚聲周尚臭固各有所尚
也苟於致祭之時而一或不謹又何以求神於
陰陽乎記郊特牲者論天子諸侯廟祭之禮如
此謂夫有虞氏之祭也以鬼神之享在誠不在
punctuated:
禮記

有虞氏之祭也，尚用氣。血腥爓，祭用氣也。殷人尚聲，臭味未成，滌蕩其聲，樂三闋，然後出迎牲。聲音之號，所以詔告於天地之間也。周人尚臭，灌用鬯臭，鬱合鬯，臭陰達於淵泉。灌以圭璋，用玉氣也。既灌，然後迎牲，致陰氣也。蕭合黍稷，臭陽達於墻屋。故既奠，然後焫蕭，合羶薌。凡祭，慎諸此。

王華

同考試官教諭吳批：此題頭緒頗多，作者類多冗泛。其「凡祭慎諸此」一句，或言單者，或言群祀，殊無定見。此篇理明詞順，尤宜高薦。
考試官教授徐批：見理明，行文暢，是用錄出。
考試官教授王批：說出歷代廟祭之禮，可取。

知歷代之致祭各有所尚，當知歷代之致祭各謹所尚。盖虞尚氣，殷尚聲，周尚臭，固各有所尚也。苟於致祭之時，而一或不謹，又何以求神於陰陽乎？記郊特牲者，論天子諸侯廟祭之禮如此。謂夫有虞氏之祭也，以鬼神之享在誠不在
translation_en:
Record of Rites

“In the sacrifices of the house of Yu, emphasis was placed on vapor. Offering blood, raw flesh, and scalded flesh was the use of vapor in sacrifice. The people of Yin emphasized sound. Before the smells and flavors were ready, they sent forth the sound of their music far and wide. After three performances of the music, they went out to welcome the sacrificial animal. The proclamation through sound served to announce the sacrifice throughout the space between Heaven and Earth. The people of Zhou emphasized fragrance. For the libation they used the fragrance of aromatic millet wine, blending it with turmeric; its fragrance reached downward through the yin to the deep springs. They poured the libation using gui and zhang jade implements, employing the emanations of jade. Only after the libation did they welcome the sacrificial animal: this brought forth the yin emanations. Southernwood was combined with millet and panicled millet, and its fragrance rose through the yang to the walls and roofs. Thus, after setting out the offerings, they burned southernwood, combining the aromas of fat and grain. In every sacrifice, care must be taken over these things.”

Wang Hua

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: This topic has quite a few threads, and most writers become prolix and vague. As for the sentence ‘In every sacrifice, care must be taken over these things,’ some speak of a single sacrifice [?], while others speak of the various sacrifices, with no settled interpretation. This essay is clear in its reasoning and fluent in its expression; it particularly merits recommendation for a high ranking.

Comment by Examiner Xu, Professor: His understanding of the principles is clear, and his writing flows smoothly. For this reason, the essay has been selected for inclusion.

Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: It elucidates the rites of ancestral-temple sacrifice under successive dynasties and is worthy of selection.

Knowing that successive dynasties each emphasized something particular in performing sacrifices, one should also understand that each carefully attended to what it emphasized. Yu emphasized vapor, Yin sound, and Zhou fragrance: each certainly had its own emphasis. If, when performing sacrifices, they were careless in even one respect, how could they seek the spirits in yin and yang? The author of ‘The Single Victim at the Suburban Sacrifice’ discusses in this way the ancestral-temple sacrificial rites of the Son of Heaven and the feudal lords. The meaning is that, in the sacrifices of the house of Yu, the spirits’ acceptance of the offerings depended upon sincerity and not upon…

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
味故以氣為尚焉觀其先薦以血而詔神於室
次薦腥爓而詔神於堂是欲以誠敬之心交神
於冥漠非尚氣而何殷人之祭也以聲音之感
無間乎顯幽故以聲為尚焉觀其犧牲未陳必
先作樂於廟庭樂音三闋然後迎牲於廟外是
欲以聲音之號詔告於兩間非尚聲而何以至
周人之祭則又尚乎臭焉故夫方祭之初必灌
地以鬯而香氣為之芬芳和鬯以鬱而香氣為
之滋甚使臭陰之氣下達於淵泉矣然灌以圭
===
璋而用玉之氣灌後迎牲而致氣於陰非尚其
臭之陰者乎既灌之餘取彼香蒿以雜夫牲牢
之脂合彼黍稷以爇於爐炭之上使臭陽之氣
達於墻屋矣然斯禮也又必宗祝酌酒之既奠
然後蕭合黍稷之是爇非尚其臭之陽者乎是
則尚氣尚聲固所以求神於陰陽也使或不謹
其何以格於神乎故凡有事於太廟莫不一謹
乎此而無慢易之心焉周人尚臭亦所以求神
於陰陽也使或不慎抑何以交於神乎故凡祀
punctuated: 味，故以氣為尚焉。觀其先薦以血而詔神於室，次薦腥爓而詔神於堂，是欲以誠敬之心交神於冥漠，非尚氣而何？殷人之祭也，以聲音之感無間乎顯幽，故以聲為尚焉。觀其犧牲未陳，必先作樂於廟庭，樂音三闋，然後迎牲於廟外，是欲以聲音之號詔告於兩間，非尚聲而何？以至周人之祭，則又尚乎臭焉。故夫方祭之初，必灌地以鬯，而香氣為之芬芳；和鬯以鬱，而香氣為之滋甚，使臭陰之氣下達於淵泉矣。然灌以圭璋而用玉之氣，灌後迎牲而致氣於陰，非尚其臭之陰者乎？既灌之餘，取彼香蒿以雜夫牲牢之脂，合彼黍稷以爇於爐炭之上，使臭陽之氣達於墻屋矣。然斯禮也，又必宗祝酌酒之既奠，然後蕭合黍稷之是爇，非尚其臭之陽者乎？是則尚氣尚聲，固所以求神於陰陽也。使或不謹，其何以格於神乎？故凡有事於太廟，莫不一謹乎此，而無慢易之心焉。周人尚臭，亦所以求神於陰陽也。使或不慎，抑何以交於神乎？故凡祀
translation_en:
…flavor; hence they gave precedence to vital emanations. Consider how they first offered blood to summon the spirits in the inner chamber, then offered raw and partially cooked meat to summon them in the hall. Their purpose was to commune with the spirits in the unseen realm through a sincere and reverent heart. Was this not giving precedence to vital emanations?

In the sacrifices of the Yin people, the influence of sound passed unhindered between the visible and invisible realms; hence they gave precedence to sound. Consider how, before the sacrificial animals were set out, they first performed music in the ancestral temple courtyard. Only after three movements of music did they go outside the temple to receive the animals. Their purpose was to announce their summons through sound throughout the space between Heaven and Earth. Was this not giving precedence to sound?

As for the sacrifices of the Zhou people, they gave precedence to fragrance. Thus, at the very beginning of the sacrifice, they poured aromatic sacrificial liquor onto the ground, releasing its sweet scent. They mixed the liquor with turmeric, making its fragrance still more intense, so that the fragrant emanations associated with yin descended to the deep springs. They performed the libation with vessels fitted with gui and zhang jade tablets, employing the emanations of jade; after the libation, they received the sacrificial animals, conveying their emanations to the yin realm. Was this not giving precedence to fragrance in its yin aspect?

After the libation, they took fragrant southernwood and mixed it with the fat of the sacrificial animals, combined it with glutinous and non-glutinous millet, and burned it over charcoal in a brazier, so that the fragrant emanations associated with yang reached the walls and roofs. Yet in this rite, too, they had to wait until the invocator had poured and presented the wine before burning the southernwood mixed with millet. Was this not giving precedence to fragrance in its yang aspect?

Thus, giving precedence to vital emanations and to sound were indeed means of seeking the spirits in yin and yang. If care were lacking in any respect, how could one reach the spirits? Therefore, whenever rites were performed in the Grand Ancestral Temple, everyone exercised the utmost care in these matters, without any irreverence or carelessness of heart. The Zhou people's precedence for fragrance likewise served to seek the spirits in yin and yang. If vigilance were lacking in any respect, how could one commune with the spirits? title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
乎其先莫不一慎乎此而無怠忽之意焉吁古
人致謹於宗廟之禮也如此宜記者記之以示
人也歟抑考禮經言致祭之義不一而足有以
求陰求陽言之者有以正祭祊祭言之者豈知
神之所享於此乎於彼乎亦不過仁人孝子之
心自盡其誠敬焉耳故曰鬼神無常享享於克
誠其此之謂歟
禮樂明備天地官矣
蔡錬
===
同考試官教諭呉批此題一本上文立説塲中作者於明備處多專以五聲六律三千三百為講殊失本旨詞簡理明僅見此篇
考試官教授徐批發明禮樂造化相為流通之妙可取
考試官教授王批辭理俱到可取
惟制作極其妙斯造化得其職夫造化禮樂相
為流通者也禮樂之精微寓於制作者既極其
妙則造化之生成豈不各得其職哉今夫禮樂
之明且備不外乎天地之和與序也是故高下
散殊天地自然之序也周流同化天地自然之
punctuated:
乎其先，莫不一慎乎此，而無怠忽之意焉。吁！古人致謹於宗廟之禮也如此，宜記者記之以示人也歟！抑考禮經，言致祭之義不一而足：有以求陰求陽言之者，有以正祭祊祭言之者。豈知神之所享，於此乎？於彼乎？亦不過仁人孝子之心，自盡其誠敬焉耳。故曰：「鬼神無常享，享於克誠。」其此之謂歟！

禮樂明備，天地官矣。
蔡錬

同考試官教諭呉批：此題一本上文立説，塲中作者於明備處，多專以五聲六律、三千三百為講，殊失本旨。詞簡理明，僅見此篇。
考試官教授徐批：發明禮樂造化相為流通之妙，可取。
考試官教授王批：辭理俱到，可取。

惟制作極其妙，斯造化得其職。夫造化禮樂相為流通者也。禮樂之精微寓於制作者，既極其妙，則造化之生成豈不各得其職哉？今夫禮樂之明且備，不外乎天地之和與序也。是故高下散殊，天地自然之序也；周流同化，天地自然之
translation_en:
…in sacrificing to their ancestors, all exercised the utmost care in this, with no thought of negligence or disregard. Ah! Such was the care the ancients devoted to the rites of the ancestral temple. Surely it was fitting that the recorder should record this to instruct others! Moreover, examining the ritual classics, we find that their explanations of the meaning of offering sacrifice are too numerous to exhaust. Some speak of seeking the spirits in yin and yang; others speak of the principal sacrifice and the sacrifice at the temple gate. How could one know where the spirits receive the offerings—here or there? These practices are simply the means by which humane persons and filial sons fully express their sincerity and reverence. Thus it is said: “The spirits do not invariably accept offerings; they accept those offered with true sincerity.” Is this not what it means?

“When Rites and Music Are Manifest and Complete, Heaven and Earth Fulfill Their Offices.”
Cai Lian

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: “The argument for this topic rests entirely upon the preceding passage. In discussing ‘manifest and complete,’ many candidates in the examination confined themselves to the five tones and six pitch standards, and the three thousand and three hundred rules of ritual, thus seriously missing the original meaning. This is the only essay I have seen whose wording is concise and reasoning clear.”
Comment by Examiner Xu, Professor: “It elucidates the subtle way in which rites and music and the creative transformations of nature interconnect. Worth selecting.”
Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: “Both expression and reasoning are fully realized. Worth selecting.”

Only when the institutions established attain their utmost refinement do the creative transformations of nature fulfill their offices. The creative transformations of nature and rites and music interconnect. Once the subtle principles of rites and music embodied in what is established attain their utmost refinement, how could the generative and completing operations of nature fail each to fulfill its office? Now, the manifest completeness of rites and music consists in nothing beyond the harmony and order of Heaven and Earth. Thus, the distinctions dispersed between high and low constitute the natural order of Heaven and Earth; their all-pervading circulation and shared transformation constitute the natural …

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
和也聖人仰觀俯察有見夫天地之序默運於
秋冬者一斂藏之義而義近於禮矣由是因之
以制禮則禮以辨異而配乎地其精微之寓於
所制者豈不明且備乎天地之和流行於春夏
者一合同之仁而仁近於樂矣由是本之以作
樂則樂以敦和而應乎天其精微之寓於所作
者又不明且備乎禮樂明備如此吾見天秉陽
而位乎上固以生物為職也然陽有時而過亢
物不遂其生者有矣今樂以敦和則足以發達
===
乎陽之所生而陽不過亢故夫春而生夏而長
萬物其熙熙矣天豈有不得其職者哉地秉陰
而位乎下固以成物為職也然陰有時而過肅
物不得其成者有矣今禮以辨異則足以安定
乎陰之所成而陰不過肅故夫秋而斂冬而藏
萬物其秩秩矣地豈有不得其職者哉吁聖人
始焉法天地而為禮樂終焉以禮樂而贊天地
也有如是夫雖然天地先禮樂而形禮樂後天
地而作聖人則居其位而裁成輔相之爾觀諸
punctuated: 和也。聖人仰觀俯察，有見夫天地之序默運於秋冬者，一斂藏之義，而義近於禮矣。由是因之以制禮，則禮以辨異而配乎地，其精微之寓於所制者，豈不明且備乎？天地之和流行於春夏者，一合同之仁，而仁近於樂矣。由是本之以作樂，則樂以敦和而應乎天，其精微之寓於所作者，又不明且備乎？禮樂明備如此，吾見天秉陽而位乎上，固以生物為職也。然陽有時而過亢，物不遂其生者有矣。今樂以敦和，則足以發達乎陽之所生，而陽不過亢。故夫春而生，夏而長，萬物其熙熙矣，天豈有不得其職者哉？地秉陰而位乎下，固以成物為職也。然陰有時而過肅，物不得其成者有矣。今禮以辨異，則足以安定乎陰之所成，而陰不過肅。故夫秋而斂，冬而藏，萬物其秩秩矣，地豈有不得其職者哉？吁！聖人始焉法天地而為禮樂，終焉以禮樂而贊天地也，有如是夫！雖然，天地先禮樂而形，禮樂後天地而作，聖人則居其位而裁成輔相之爾。觀諸
translation_en:
…the natural harmony of Heaven and Earth. The sage looks upward and examines below, perceiving that the order of Heaven and Earth, silently operating in autumn and winter, is wholly the righteousness of gathering in and storing away; and righteousness is close to ritual. Accordingly, he follows this in establishing ritual. Ritual distinguishes differences and thus corresponds to Earth. Are not the subtle principles embodied in what he establishes both clear and complete? The harmony of Heaven and Earth, flowing through spring and summer, is wholly the benevolence of joining and uniting; and benevolence is close to music. Accordingly, he takes this as his basis in creating music. Music strengthens harmony and thus responds to Heaven. Are not the subtle principles embodied in what he creates likewise clear and complete?

With ritual and music thus clear and complete, I observe that Heaven embodies yang and occupies the position above, assuredly taking the generation of things as its office. Yet yang sometimes becomes excessively forceful, and there are things that fail to attain their full growth. Now music, by strengthening harmony, suffices to foster the development of what yang generates, so that yang does not become excessively forceful. Thus, as things come to life in spring and grow in summer, the myriad things flourish abundantly. How could Heaven fail to fulfill its office? Earth embodies yin and occupies the position below, assuredly taking the completion of things as its office. Yet yin sometimes becomes excessively austere, and there are things that fail to reach completion. Now ritual, by distinguishing differences, suffices to settle and secure what yin brings to completion, so that yin does not become excessively austere. Thus, as things are gathered in during autumn and stored away during winter, the myriad things are duly ordered. How could Earth fail to fulfill its office?

Ah! The sage begins by modeling himself on Heaven and Earth to establish ritual and music, and ends by assisting Heaven and Earth through ritual and music. Such is the way of it! Nevertheless, Heaven and Earth took form before ritual and music, and ritual and music were created after Heaven and Earth. The sage simply occupies his position, bringing their workings to proper completion and assisting them. If we examine…

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
上文有曰明於天地然後能興禮樂也此則曰
禮樂明備天地官矣于以見天地者禮樂之本
源禮樂者天地之妙用而聖人者禮樂之宗主
也不可不知
論
王道所以為大
李旻
同考試官訓導瞿批場中作論雅或失之陳蹈奇或失之
穿鑿此篇發明王道之大如天之自然措詞典雅筆力老健信論手也
===
同考試官學正陳批立論正大措詞高古脫凡近而見新
竒如此篇者指未許多屈也文哉文哉
考試官教授徐批寫出王道所以為大可嘉
考試官教授王批形容王道之大深得程子本旨録之以示後學
論曰德業之盛一同乎造化之自然此王
道之所以為大也盖大莫大乎天地之道
也王者過化存神之妙與之同運並行舉
一世之民皆囿於甄陶之內是其德業之
盛誠非伯功之小所能彷彿其萬一矣此
punctuated:
上文有曰：「明於天地，然後能興禮樂也。」此則曰：「禮樂明備，天地官矣。」于以見天地者禮樂之本源，禮樂者天地之妙用，而聖人者禮樂之宗主也，不可不知。
論
王道所以為大
李旻
同考試官訓導瞿批：場中作論，雅或失之陳蹈，奇或失之穿鑿。此篇發明王道之大，如天之自然，措詞典雅，筆力老健，信論手也。
同考試官學正陳批：立論正大，措詞高古，脫凡近而見新竒。如此篇者，指未許多屈也。文哉！文哉！
考試官教授徐批：寫出王道所以為大，可嘉。
考試官教授王批：形容王道之大，深得程子本旨，録之以示後學。
論曰：德業之盛，一同乎造化之自然，此王道之所以為大也。盖大莫大乎天地之道也。王者過化存神之妙，與之同運並行，舉一世之民，皆囿於甄陶之內。是其德業之盛，誠非伯功之小所能彷彿其萬一矣。此
translation_en:
…the preceding passage, which says: “Only after understanding Heaven and Earth can one institute rites and music.” Here it says: “When rites and music are clearly established and fully provided, Heaven and Earth fulfill their offices.” From this we see that Heaven and Earth are the source of rites and music, that rites and music are the wondrous operation of Heaven and Earth, and that the sage is the presiding authority over rites and music. This must be understood.
Discourse
Why the Kingly Way Is Great
Li Min 李旻
Comment by Associate Examiner Qu, Instructor: Among the discourses composed in the examination hall, those seeking elegance sometimes lapse into stale imitation, while those seeking originality sometimes lapse into strained interpretations. This piece elucidates the greatness of the Kingly Way as resembling Heaven’s spontaneous workings. Its diction is dignified and elegant, its writing seasoned and vigorous. Its author is truly a master of the discourse.
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, School Director: Its argument is upright and broad, its diction lofty and antique. It rises above the commonplace and displays freshness and originality. In counting pieces like this one, one could scarcely bend many fingers [?]. What fine writing! What fine writing!
Comment by Examiner Xu, Professor: It brings out why the Kingly Way is great. Commendable.
Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: In depicting the greatness of the Kingly Way, it profoundly grasps Master Cheng’s original meaning. It is recorded here to instruct later students.
The discourse says: The fullness of virtue and achievement accords entirely with the spontaneous workings of creation: this is why the Kingly Way is great. All the people of an age are encompassed within his molding and nurturing influence. title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
王者之道所以為大也何如哉請舉天地
之大以論王道之大天之道高也明也舉
萬物無不覆焉而凡在所覆者無一而不
遂其性地之道博也厚也舉萬物無不載
焉而凡在所載者無一而不得其所此天
地之道大矣而其所以為大者有本焉觀
其四時迭運化育流行乃天地之用一過
而無迹者也非化乎於穆之命純一不已
乃天地之心常存而不測者也非神乎惟
===
其化之大是以物各付物而各正性命之
功莫得以窺其端倪惟其神之妙是以無
聲無臭而健順生成之德莫得以測其機
括此天地之道所以為大也王者之道何
異於是彼王者之世民皆熈熈然廣大自
得相忘於帝力何有之天皡皡然安養自
如咸躋於至和氤氳之域殺之而不怨也
利之而不庸也民日遷善而不知為之者
此王道之大也然其所以為大者亦有本
punctuated:
王者之道所以為大也。何如哉？請舉天地之大，以論王道之大。天之道，高也，明也，舉萬物無不覆焉，而凡在所覆者，無一而不遂其性。地之道，博也，厚也，舉萬物無不載焉，而凡在所載者，無一而不得其所。此天地之道大矣，而其所以為大者有本焉。觀其四時迭運，化育流行，乃天地之用，一過而無迹者也，非化乎？於穆之命，純一不已，乃天地之心，常存而不測者也，非神乎？惟其化之大，是以物各付物，而各正性命之功，莫得以窺其端倪；惟其神之妙，是以無聲無臭，而健順生成之德，莫得以測其機括。此天地之道所以為大也。
王者之道何異於是？彼王者之世，民皆熈熈然廣大自得，相忘於帝力何有之天；皡皡然安養自如，咸躋於至和氤氳之域。殺之而不怨也，利之而不庸也，民日遷善，而不知為之者，此王道之大也。然其所以為大者，亦有本
translation_en:
… is why the way of the true king is great. How is this so? Let us discuss the greatness of the kingly way by considering the greatness of Heaven and Earth. The way of Heaven is lofty and bright: among the myriad things, none is beyond its covering, and of all that it covers, none fails to fulfill its nature. The way of Earth is broad and substantial: among the myriad things, none is beyond its support, and of all that it supports, none fails to find its proper place. Great indeed is this way of Heaven and Earth, yet its greatness has a foundation. Observe how the four seasons revolve in succession and the processes of transformation and nurture flow onward: this is the functioning of Heaven and Earth, passing without leaving a trace. Is this not transformation? The profound and reverent mandate, pure and undivided, never ceases: this is the heart of Heaven and Earth, ever present yet unfathomable. Is this not spiritual efficacy? Precisely because their transformation is great, each thing is left to itself, and no one can discern the workings by which each attains its proper nature and allotted destiny. Precisely because their spiritual efficacy is wondrous, they are without sound or scent, and no one can fathom the mechanism of their power to generate and complete things through vigor and receptivity. This is why the way of Heaven and Earth is great.
How does the way of the true king differ from this? In the age of a true king, the people are all joyful, expansive, and content, oblivious to imperial power beneath a heaven where they ask, “What has the emperor’s power to do with us?” In simple purity they live at ease, nurtured and secure, all entering a realm suffused with the utmost harmony. When he puts them to death, they bear no resentment; when he benefits them, they do not credit him with the service. Daily the people advance toward goodness without knowing who brings this about. Such is the greatness of the kingly way. Yet its greatness, too, has a foundation …

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
焉蓋王者之道即天地之道王者之心即
天地之心凡身所經歷處即人無不化如
雷一震而萬物生動霜一降而萬物成實
蓋不待久於此而深治之焉凡心所存主
處便神妙莫測不疾而速猶聲響之相應
不行而至猶形影之相隨有莫知其所以
然而然者焉是以殺之不怨者因民之所
惡而去之非有心於殺之也利之不庸者
因民之所利而利之非有心於利之也民
===
日遷善而不知為之者亦惟輔其性之自
然使自得之耳抑何容心於其間哉此王
道之所以為大也故上焉而與大哉乾元
萬物資始之化而同運舉一世而甄陶無
遺視彼伯者但致民一時之驩虞不過小
小補其罅隙而已比之王道奚啻泰山之
於丘垤哉此王道之所以為大也下焉而
與至哉坤元萬物資生之化而並行合八
荒而皆在我闥視彼伯者但急民一時之
punctuated: 焉。蓋王者之道即天地之道，王者之心即天地之心。凡身所經歷處，即人無不化，如雷一震而萬物生動，霜一降而萬物成實，蓋不待久於此而深治之焉。凡心所存主處，便神妙莫測，不疾而速，猶聲響之相應；不行而至，猶形影之相隨，有莫知其所以然而然者焉。是以殺之不怨者，因民之所惡而去之，非有心於殺之也；利之不庸者，因民之所利而利之，非有心於利之也。民日遷善而不知為之者，亦惟輔其性之自然，使自得之耳，抑何容心於其間哉？此王道之所以為大也。故上焉而與「大哉乾元，萬物資始」之化而同運，舉一世而甄陶無遺。視彼伯者，但致民一時之驩虞，不過小小補其罅隙而已，比之王道，奚啻泰山之於丘垤哉？此王道之所以為大也。下焉而與「至哉坤元，萬物資生」之化而並行，合八荒而皆在我闥。視彼伯者，但急民一時之
translation_en: …therein. For the way of the true king is the way of Heaven and Earth, and the heart of the true king is the heart of Heaven and Earth. Wherever he passes in person, none among the people fails to be transformed [?], just as a single peal of thunder brings the myriad things to life and motion, and a single descent of frost brings them to maturity and fruition. He need not remain there long and govern them intensively. Wherever his heart directs its attention, its efficacy is wondrous and unfathomable: swift without haste, like the answering of an echo to a sound; arriving without traveling, like a shadow following a form. These things happen without anyone knowing how they come about. Thus, when he puts people to death and incurs no resentment, it is because he removes what the people detest, without any deliberate desire to kill. When he benefits them and they give him no credit, it is because he benefits them through what they themselves find beneficial, without any deliberate desire to confer benefits. When the people advance daily toward goodness without knowing who brings this about, he merely assists the natural workings of their nature, enabling them to attain it for themselves. How could any contrived intention enter into this? This is why the kingly way is great. Thus, above, it operates together with the transforming power described in the words, “Great indeed is the primal power of Qian! The myriad things depend upon it for their beginning,” molding the whole age without leaving anything out. Consider those hegemons: they merely bring the people temporary delight, doing no more than patching a few cracks. In comparing them with the kingly way, how could even the contrast between Mount Tai and a little mound suffice? This is why the kingly way is great. Below, it proceeds together with the transforming power described in the words, “Perfect indeed is the primal power of Kun! The myriad things depend upon it for their birth,” gathering all the eight distant regions within my gates. Consider those hegemons: they merely concern themselves urgently with the people's momentary…

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
功利不過小小塞其滲漏而已較之王道
奚啻河海之於行潦哉此王道之所以為
大也吁天地之道難於形容即其功用之
廣大而見其神化之妙王者之道難於名
狀即其德業之盛大而見其神化之速天
地一王者也王者一天地也孰謂王道之
所以為大有不同於天地之所以為大乎
稽之往古堯舜之帝天下禹湯文武之王
天下當是之時黎民於變四方風動民協
===
于中會其有極固皆純乎王道之流行然
當時之民不識不知順帝之則而已孰知
王道之大也未始有伯抑孰知伯功之小
也逮夫世道日降王道變而為伯圖矣人
心陷溺但知有伯功之小而不知有王道
之大矣又豈知王道之所以為大哉孟子
生於戰國拳拳於王伯之辨所以正人心
扶世道其功誠不在禹下千載而下朱子
因孟子之意而發明王道之所以為大則
punctuated: 功利，不過小小塞其滲漏而已。較之王道，奚啻河海之於行潦哉！此王道之所以為大也。吁！天地之道難於形容，即其功用之廣大而見其神化之妙；王者之道難於名狀，即其德業之盛大而見其神化之速。天地，一王者也；王者，一天地也。孰謂王道之所以為大，有不同於天地之所以為大乎？稽之往古，堯舜之帝天下，禹湯文武之王天下，當是之時，黎民於變，四方風動，民協于中，會其有極，固皆純乎王道之流行。然當時之民，不識不知，順帝之則而已。孰知王道之大也？未始有伯，抑孰知伯功之小也？逮夫世道日降，王道變而為伯圖矣。人心陷溺，但知有伯功之小，而不知有王道之大矣，又豈知王道之所以為大哉？孟子生於戰國，拳拳於王伯之辨，所以正人心、扶世道，其功誠不在禹下。千載而下，朱子因孟子之意，而發明王道之所以為大，則
translation_en:
…benefit and advantage, doing no more than plugging a few small leaks. Compared with the Kingly Way, is the disparity not even greater than that between rivers and seas and puddles on a road? This is why the Kingly Way is great. Ah! The Way of Heaven and Earth is difficult to describe, yet the vast scope of its workings reveals the subtlety of its wondrous transformations. The Way of the true king is difficult to put into words, yet the grandeur of his virtue and achievements reveals the swiftness of his wondrous transforming influence. Heaven and Earth are a true king; a true king is Heaven and Earth. Who could say that what makes the Kingly Way great differs from what makes Heaven and Earth great?

Looking back to antiquity, when Yao and Shun ruled all under Heaven as emperors, and Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu ruled all under Heaven as kings, the common people were transformed, and the four quarters stirred as if moved by the wind. The people conformed to the mean and gathered around the supreme standard. All this was assuredly the unalloyed operation of the Kingly Way. Yet the people of that time, without conscious understanding or knowledge, simply followed the Lord on High’s rules. Who understood the greatness of the Kingly Way? Since there had not yet been hegemons, who could have known the pettiness of hegemonic achievements? When the moral condition of the world declined day by day, the Kingly Way changed into schemes for hegemony. Human hearts became engulfed in corruption: people knew only the petty achievements of hegemons and no longer knew the greatness of the Kingly Way. How, then, could they understand why the Kingly Way is great?

Mengzi, born in the Warring States period, devoted himself earnestly to distinguishing true kingship from hegemony, thereby rectifying human hearts and sustaining the moral order of the world. His achievement was truly no less than Yu’s. More than a thousand years later, Master Zhu, following Mengzi’s meaning, elucidated why the Kingly Way is great; thus …

text:
又有功於孟子者也旴二帝三王遠矣純
乎王道而斯世斯民皥皥如也愚何幸躬
逢

===

伏以
貳秩台衡居廟堂之要地參知鼎實預軍
國之訏謨豈直藉夫虚名盖將收其實用
幹樞弗稱覆餗貽羞伏念臣仲淹猥以吳
下迂疎竊慕古人風節早膺剡薦謬列諫
司冀輔德於
宸衷曽敷言論動獲尤於當道幾至竄投驅
策塞垣微勞莫効運籌宥省
punctuated:
又有功於孟子者也。旴！二帝三王遠矣，純乎王道，而斯世斯民皥皥如也。愚何幸躬逢聖明之世！

translation_en:
…he, too, rendered a service to Mencius. Ah[?]! The Two Emperors and Three Kings are far distant now. Their rule was purely the Kingly Way, and the people of that age lived in contented ease. How fortunate am I, unworthy though I am, to live in an age of sagely and enlightened rule!

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
渙寵有加兹盖伏遇
〇〇〇〇
堯德聰明
禹躬勤儉纘承
大統允迪
前徽惇四海之民彝壽
萬年之國脉九居覆載溥荷生成銳意太平
留心耆舊過聽諫官之論遽叨執政之遷
雖簡任榮殊自知踰分而賛襄責重未允
===
固辭臣敢不力奮駑庸惟切劘之是效誓
殫鯁直以阿曲而自懲用圖庶績之熈勉
决六聯之滯先憂後樂期不負于素心外
攘內安庶少酬於
洪造臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以

translation_en:
…Your abundant favor has increased still further. This is because I have humbly encountered 〇〇〇〇 [four circle marks in the text], whose virtue is enlightened like Yao’s and whose personal conduct is diligent and frugal like Yu’s. You have succeeded to the great imperial line and faithfully followed the splendid example of your predecessors, strengthening the enduring moral bonds among the people within the Four Seas and prolonging the life of the state for ten thousand years. All the nine regions [?], beneath Heaven and upon Earth, abundantly receive your nurturing bounty. Intent upon great peace and mindful of elderly, experienced servants, you have given undue credence to the remonstrance officials’ arguments and suddenly favored me with promotion to the ranks of those directing government. Although this selection confers exceptional honor, I know that it exceeds my deserts; yet, weighty as the responsibility of assisting your rule is, you have not permitted me firmly to decline.
How could your servant fail to exert his dull and mediocre abilities, striving only to offer searching counsel? title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄

國朝之制一貫帝王之道且事實不遺文辭精采非纒問目者比
考試官教授徐批君道一策鋪叙有條是宜錄出

朝

第一問
侯聘

Policy Essay
First Question
Hou Pin

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: He understands that the institutions of our dynasty embody the same Way as the emperors and kings of antiquity. Moreover, he omits none of the facts, and his language is polished and vivid. This cannot be compared with essays that merely entangle themselves in the wording of the question.

Examiner Xu, Professor, comments: This policy essay on the Way of the ruler develops its exposition in an orderly fashion. It deserves to be selected for inclusion.

Examiner Wang, Professor, comments: This policy essay answers each point fully and clearly. It certainly merits a high recommendation.

The sages of earlier times arose in succession, establishing laws and transmitting teachings to serve as models for a hundred generations; the sages of later times followed them, setting forth pronouncements and bequeathing instructions to display the cultural brilliance of their age.

Whenever a dynasty arises, it necessarily has institutions of its own. The Two Emperors and Three Kings arose successively in earlier times and established laws and transmitted teachings to provide models for a hundred generations. The successive sage rulers of our dynasty have followed them: surely their pronouncements and enduring instructions serve to manifest the culturally enlightened government of this age? I respectfully set forth my reply.

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
慎徽五典而五典克從禹之文命四敷而
不距朕行湯之肇脩人紀而兆民允殖文
王緝熈敬止而萬民咸和武王重民五教
而四海永清是已下逮漢唐宋皆於斯道
有所未盡姑置無論洪惟我
太祖高皇帝肇造區夏御製大誥三編訓飭臣
民
太宗文皇帝輯寧邦家御製為善陰隲孝順事
實二書以勉人為善為孝
===
宣宗章皇帝繼體守成御製五倫一書以教人
明倫觀大誥所載若唐鐸為善之最則彰
之以示勸郭桓為惡之尤則癉之以示懲
為善陰隲所載不妄殺一人而其女為后
者鄧禹也辯孝婦之寃而後昆以興者非
于定國乎孝順事實所載負罪引慝而克
諧以孝者舜也一日三朝而問安視膳者
非文王乎至若五倫書所載見於聖德篇
若生而神靈弱而能言而具敦敏聰明之
punctuated:
慎徽五典，而五典克從；禹之文命四敷，而不距朕行；湯之肇脩人紀，而兆民允殖；文王緝熈敬止，而萬民咸和；武王重民五教，而四海永清，是已。下逮漢唐宋，皆於斯道有所未盡，姑置無論。洪惟我太祖高皇帝肇造區夏，御製《大誥》三編，訓飭臣民。太宗文皇帝輯寧邦家，御製《為善陰隲》《孝順事實》二書，以勉人為善、為孝。宣宗章皇帝繼體守成，御製《五倫》一書，以教人明倫。
觀《大誥》所載，若唐鐸為善之最，則彰之以示勸；郭桓為惡之尤，則癉之以示懲。《為善陰隲》所載，不妄殺一人而其女為后者，鄧禹也；辯孝婦之寃而後昆以興者，非于定國乎？《孝順事實》所載，負罪引慝而克諧以孝者，舜也；一日三朝而問安視膳者，非文王乎？至若《五倫書》所載，見於《聖德篇》，若生而神靈、弱而能言，而具敦敏聰明之
translation_en:
…carefully promoted the five cardinal teachings, and these teachings were duly followed; Yu spread his civilizing instruction throughout the four quarters, and none opposed his conduct; Tang first cultivated the bonds of human relations, and the myriad people truly flourished; King Wen continuously illuminated his virtue and dwelt in reverence, and all the people lived in harmony; King Wu esteemed the five teachings for the people, and all within the four seas enjoyed lasting peace. These are examples of this. Coming down to the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties, all fell short in some respect in pursuing this Way; let us leave them aside without discussion for now. We reverently consider how our Emperor Taizu Gao founded the realm and imperially composed the three compilations of the Grand Pronouncements (Da gao) to instruct and admonish officials and commoners. Emperor Taizong Wen brought peace to the state and imperially composed the two books Doing Good and Its Hidden Recompense (Wei shan yin zhi) and True Accounts of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun shishi), to encourage people to do good and practice filial piety. Emperor Xuanzong Zhang succeeded to the throne and preserved the inherited achievement, imperially composing the Five Human Relationships (Wulun) to teach people to understand those relationships.
Looking at what the Grand Pronouncements records, someone such as Tang Duo, outstanding in doing good, is commended to encourage others; someone such as Guo Huan, extreme in wrongdoing, is condemned to warn others. Among those recorded in Doing Good and Its Hidden Recompense, the man who did not wantonly kill a single person and whose daughter became empress was Deng Yu. Was not the man who vindicated a filial woman unjustly accused, and whose descendants consequently prospered, Yu Dingguo? Among those recorded in True Accounts of Filial Obedience, the man who took guilt and wrongdoing upon himself and achieved harmony through filial piety was Shun. Was not the man who attended his father three times a day, inquiring after his health and seeing to his meals, King Wen? As for what is recorded in the Book of the Five Human Relationships, in the chapter “Sage Virtue,” there is the example of one who was divinely gifted from birth and could speak while still an infant, and who possessed earnestness, quick understanding, and keen intelligence…

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
德者此黃帝之盡君道也見於輔德篇若
慎厥身脩思永后從諫則聖以致責難陳
善之敬者此皐陶傅說之盡臣道也伯禽
三見周公而三笞子路養親負米於百里
其篤父子之倫為何如堯妻舜而釐降媯
汭劉庭式娶瞽而守義不貳其全夫婦之
倫又何如他如王琳自縛詣賊免弟於難
趙孝遇盜請代脫兄於烹非全兄弟之倫
者乎符融一見郭林宗於京師而輒然嗟服
===
朱熹一扣蔡元定所學稱為老友非全師
友之倫者乎吁厚彝倫以盡參賛之功而
神功聖德掀揭乎宇宙聚精神以建經綸之業
而
御翰宸章輝映乎日星囿斯民於德化之中躋
斯世於仁壽之域是則
列聖之立言垂訓與堯之親睦九族舜之慎徽
五典禹之文命四敷湯之肇脩人紀文之
緝熈敬止武之重民五教無非欲使民各
punctuated:
德者，此黃帝之盡君道也。見於輔德篇，若「慎厥身，脩思永」、「后從諫則聖」，以致責難陳善之敬者，此皐陶、傅說之盡臣道也。伯禽三見周公而三笞，子路養親負米於百里，其篤父子之倫為何如？堯妻舜而釐降媯汭，劉庭式娶瞽而守義不貳，其全夫婦之倫又何如？他如王琳自縛詣賊，免弟於難；趙孝遇盜請代，脫兄於烹，非全兄弟之倫者乎？符融一見郭林宗於京師而輒然嗟服，朱熹一扣蔡元定所學，稱為老友，非全師友之倫者乎？
吁！厚彝倫以盡參賛之功，而神功聖德掀揭乎宇宙；聚精神以建經綸之業，而御翰宸章輝映乎日星。囿斯民於德化之中，躋斯世於仁壽之域。是則列聖之立言垂訓，與堯之親睦九族、舜之慎徽五典、禹之文命四敷、湯之肇脩人紀、文之緝熈敬止、武之重民五教，無非欲使民各
translation_en:
…virtues: this is how the Yellow Emperor fulfilled the Way of the ruler. As recorded in the chapter “Assisting Virtue,” the admonitions “Be watchful over your person; cultivate yourself and think of the long term” and “A sovereign who follows remonstrance becomes a sage” exemplify the reverence shown by demanding difficult achievements of one’s ruler and setting forth what is good. This is how Gao Yao and Fu Yue fulfilled the Way of the minister. Bo Qin visited the Duke of Zhou three times and was caned three times; Zilu carried rice a hundred li to support his parents. How deep was their devotion to the relationship between father and son! Yao gave his daughters in marriage to Shun, sending them down to the bend of the Gui River; Liu Tingshi married a blind woman and upheld his duty without wavering. How fully they fulfilled the relationship between husband and wife! Other examples include Wang Lin, who bound himself and went to the bandits to save his younger brother from danger, and Zhao Xiao, who encountered robbers and asked to take his elder brother’s place, saving him from being cooked. Did they not fulfill the relationship between brothers? Fu Rong, upon first meeting Guo Linzong in the capital, immediately exclaimed in admiration [?]; Zhu Xi, upon first questioning Cai Yuanding about his learning, called him an old friend. Did they not fulfill the relationships of teachers and friends?
Ah! By strengthening the enduring human relationships, they fully accomplished the work of assisting Heaven and Earth, and their wondrous achievements and sagely virtue rose high throughout the universe. By concentrating their spiritual energies, they established the work of ordering the realm, and their imperial writings shone alongside the sun and stars. They encompassed the people within the transforming influence of virtue and raised the world into a realm of benevolence and longevity. title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
安其道也先聖後聖豈不異世而同一揆
哉愚生佩服
聖訓于茲有年若欲為子必須舜文是法以求
盡其孝若欲為臣必須皋傅是效以求盡
其忠期上不負所教下不負所學也管見
如斯未知執事以為然否
第二問
李旻
同考試官訓導瞿批西銘一策義理玄微此篇敷答
===
詳明必邃於理學者可采
同考試官學正陳批條達詳明蓋嘗究心於性理者
考試官教授徐批善言理一分殊非究心性理者不能高薦奚忝
考試官教授王批能答出西銘之旨宜寘前列
誦西銘之言不能不疑其異究西銘之旨
不可不會其同蓋會其理之同則西銘之
旨以明而所言之異者可以無疑矣敬因
明問所及而條陳之橫渠張先生學古力
行篤志好禮為關中士子宗師嘗於學堂
punctuated:
安其道也。先聖後聖，豈不異世而同一揆哉？愚生佩服聖訓，于茲有年。若欲為子，必須舜文是法，以求盡其孝；若欲為臣，必須皋傅是效，以求盡其忠。期上不負所教，下不負所學也。管見如斯，未知執事以為然否？

第二問
李旻

同考試官訓導瞿批：西銘一策，義理玄微，此篇敷答詳明，必邃於理學者，可采。
同考試官學正陳批：條達詳明，蓋嘗究心於性理者。
考試官教授徐批：善言理一分殊，非究心性理者不能，高薦奚忝？
考試官教授王批：能答出西銘之旨，宜寘前列。

誦西銘之言，不能不疑其異；究西銘之旨，不可不會其同。蓋會其理之同，則西銘之旨以明，而所言之異者可以無疑矣。敬因明問所及而條陳之。橫渠張先生，學古力行，篤志好禮，為關中士子宗師，嘗於學堂
translation_en:
…each rest secure in their proper Way. Though the earlier and later sages lived in different ages, did they not follow the same standard? For years now, I, this humble student, have reverently embraced the imperial instructions. To fulfill my role as a son, I must take Shun and King Wen as models, seeking to discharge my filial duty fully; to fulfill my role as a minister, I must emulate Gao Yao and Fu Yue, seeking to discharge my loyalty fully. My hope is that, above, I will not fail the instruction bestowed upon me and, below, I will not betray what I have learned. Such is my narrow view; I do not know whether you, sir, consider it correct.

Second Question
Li Min 李旻

Comment by Associate Examiner Qu, Assistant Instructor: The principles involved in this policy question on the Western Inscription are profound and subtle. This essay develops its answer fully and clearly. Its author must be deeply versed in the Learning of Principle; it merits selection.

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: Well organized, thorough, and clear. The author has evidently devoted himself to investigating human nature and principle.

Comment by Examiner Xu, Professor: He explains well how principle is one while its particular allotments differ. Only someone who has devoted himself to investigating human nature and principle could do this. How could a high recommendation be undeserved?

Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: He successfully brings out the meaning of the Western Inscription in his answer and should be placed among the foremost.

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
雙牖左書砭愚右書訂頑程伊川見之謂
啓争端因改為東西二銘且謂訂頑之言
極純無雜秦漢以来學者未到又謂訂頑
一篇意極完備乃仁之體也學者其體此
意令有諸己則日用酬酢無往而非此理
之流行矣又謂西銘乃原道之宗祖蓋孟
子之後只有原道一篇原道言率性之謂
道西銘則無天命之性而言之也又謂弘
而不毅則難立毅而不弘則無以居之觀
===
子厚所作西銘則是能養浩然之氣者也
尹彦明見伊川半載後方得看西銘楊中
立答伊川往復書辨終有未釋然者蓋以
西銘之㫖隱奥而難知也紫陽朱子又謂
西銘前一段如棋盤後一段如人下棋自
乾父坤母至顛連無告非如棋盤乎自于
之翼也以下非如人下棋乎又謂西銘有
箇直劈下底道理又有箇横截斷底道理
蓋謂毎句直下而觀之事天事親之理皆
punctuated: 雙牖左書《砭愚》，右書《訂頑》。程伊川見之，謂啓争端，因改為東西二銘。且謂：「《訂頑》之言，極純無雜，秦漢以来學者未到。」又謂：「《訂頑》一篇，意極完備，乃仁之體也。學者其體此意，令有諸己，則日用酬酢，無往而非此理之流行矣。」又謂：「《西銘》乃《原道》之宗祖。蓋孟子之後，只有《原道》一篇。《原道》言率性之謂道，《西銘》則無天命之性而言之也。」又謂：「弘而不毅則難立，毅而不弘則無以居之。觀子厚所作《西銘》，則是能養浩然之氣者也。」尹彦明見伊川半載後，方得看《西銘》。楊中立答伊川往復書辨，終有未釋然者，蓋以《西銘》之㫖隱奥而難知也。紫陽朱子又謂：「《西銘》前一段如棋盤，後一段如人下棋。」自「乾父坤母」至「顛連無告」，非如棋盤乎？自「于之翼也」以下，非如人下棋乎？又謂：「《西銘》有箇直劈下底道理，又有箇横截斷底道理。」蓋謂毎句直下而觀之，事天事親之理皆
translation_en:
…at the two windows, he inscribed Admonishing Folly (Bian yu) on the left and Correcting Obstinacy (Ding wan) on the right. Cheng Yichuan saw them and said that the titles would provoke contention; they were therefore renamed the Eastern and Western Inscriptions. He also said: “The words of Correcting Obstinacy are utterly pure and unmixed, attaining what scholars since the Qin and Han have not reached.” He further said: “Correcting Obstinacy is completely comprehensive in its meaning: it embodies benevolence. If students embody this meaning and make it their own, then in their everyday dealings there will be nowhere that this principle does not flow and operate.” He also said: “The Western Inscription is the progenitor of An Inquiry into the Way (Yuan dao). Since Mengzi, there has been only that one essay, An Inquiry into the Way. An Inquiry into the Way speaks of ‘following one’s nature being called the Way,’ whereas the Western Inscription discusses it without the nature conferred by Heaven [?].” He further said: “Without resolve, broad-mindedness finds it difficult to stand firm; without broad-mindedness, resolve has no ground on which to abide. Judging from the Western Inscription that Zihou composed, he was someone capable of nourishing his vast, flowing vital energy.”

Only after half a year of studying with Yichuan was Yin Yanming allowed to read the Western Inscription. Yang Zhongli debated it in an exchange of letters with Yichuan, yet in the end some matters remained unresolved for him. This was because the purport of the Western Inscription is profound and difficult to understand. Master Zhu of Ziyang also said: “The first section of the Western Inscription is like a go board; the latter section is like someone playing go.” From “Qian is father and Kun is mother” to “those in distress with no one to appeal to”—is this not like a go board? From “the wings of … [?]” onward—is this not like someone playing go? He also said: “The Western Inscription has a line of reasoning that cuts straight down, and another that cuts across horizontally.” This means that, when each sentence is considered vertically, the principles of serving Heaven and serving one’s parents are both …

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
在焉全篇中斷而觀之則上專是事天下
專是事親各有攸屬也是書雖規模宏大
其大指前一節明人為天地之子後一節
言人事天地當如子之事父母子朱子所
謂推親親之厚以大無我之公因事親之
誠以明事天之道正此意也求其一言足
以盡蓋其義豈非程子所謂理一分殊乎
性理之學愚生冥然莫知惟執事進教之
第三問
===
李旻
同考試官訓導瞿 批 此策場中多不知事實是篇歷叙
擇將之方與古之帝王駕御英豪驅用群策而成豐偉之功舉無
遺漏非留心於史學者不能健羨健羨
同考試官學正陳 批 此答擇將事蹟歷歷不遺真強
學待問者可取可取
考試官教授徐 批 考據精審條對詳明策手也
考試官教授王 批 答將才策無踰此篇
折衝禦侮以衛國家者在將之得人分閫
punctuated:
在焉。全篇中斷而觀之，則上專是事天，下專是事親，各有攸屬也。是書雖規模宏大，其大指，前一節明人為天地之子，後一節言人事天地當如子之事父母。子朱子所謂「推親親之厚，以大無我之公；因事親之誠，以明事天之道」，正此意也。求其一言足以盡蓋其義，豈非程子所謂「理一分殊」乎？性理之學，愚生冥然莫知，惟執事進教之。
第三問
李旻
同考試官訓導瞿批：此策場中多不知事實，是篇歷叙擇將之方，與古之帝王駕御英豪、驅用群策而成豐偉之功，舉無遺漏。非留心於史學者不能。健羨！健羨！
同考試官學正陳批：此答擇將事蹟，歷歷不遺，真強學待問者。可取！可取！
考試官教授徐批：考據精審，條對詳明，策手也。
考試官教授王批：答將才策，無踰此篇。
折衝禦侮以衛國家者，在將之得人；分閫
translation_en:
…are present therein. If one divides the whole text at its midpoint, the upper portion deals exclusively with serving Heaven, and the lower exclusively with serving one’s parents: each has its particular subject. Although this work is grand in scope, its main purport is that the first section explains how human beings are the children of Heaven and Earth, while the second says that people should serve Heaven and Earth as children serve their parents. Master Zhu Xi’s statement, “Extend the deep affection felt for one’s kin to enlarge the impartiality that knows no self; draw upon sincerity in serving one’s parents to illuminate the Way of serving Heaven,” expresses precisely this meaning. If we seek a single saying sufficient to encompass its entire meaning, is it not Master Cheng’s “Principle is one, but its particular manifestations are distinct”? As for the learning of human nature and principle, I, an ignorant student, remain benighted and without understanding. I ask only that you further instruct me.
Third Policy Question
Li Min

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
授鉞以善任使者在君之知人盖將所以
統乎兵而君所以將乎將將不得人則無
運用之術固無以統乎兵君不知將則無
駕馭之道又何以用夫將哉請條陳之自
古國家雖當太平隆盛之世不忘思患預
防之心故必擇將於無事之日用將於有
事之時然其所以擇之之道則不拘拘於
一途亦惟審其材之可用而用之也如管
仲舉於射鉤孟明舉於敗績此不以罪而
===
見廢也穰苴拔於寒微吳起拔於羈旅此
不以遠而見遺也蘇秦之合從張儀之連
衡曷嘗以詐而踈哉衛青起自人奴去病
起自假子曷嘗以賤而棄哉是皆用其所
長而棄其所短也夫選將以五材為體所
謂智信仁勇嚴是也以五謹為用所謂理
備果戒約是也其曰必死可殺必生可虜
忿速可侮廉潔可辱愛民可煩非五危之
謂乎其曰不量眾寡本乏刑德失於訓練
punctuated:
授鉞以善任使者，在君之知人。盖將所以統乎兵，而君所以將乎將。將不得人，則無運用之術，固無以統乎兵；君不知將，則無駕馭之道，又何以用夫將哉？請條陳之。
自古國家雖當太平隆盛之世，不忘思患預防之心，故必擇將於無事之日，用將於有事之時。然其所以擇之之道，則不拘拘於一途，亦惟審其材之可用而用之也。如管仲舉於射鉤，孟明舉於敗績，此不以罪而見廢也；穰苴拔於寒微，吳起拔於羈旅，此不以遠而見遺也。蘇秦之合從，張儀之連衡，曷嘗以詐而踈哉？衛青起自人奴，去病起自假子，曷嘗以賤而棄哉？是皆用其所長而棄其所短也。
夫選將以五材為體，所謂智、信、仁、勇、嚴是也；以五謹為用，所謂理、備、果、戒、約是也。其曰「必死可殺，必生可虜，忿速可侮，廉潔可辱，愛民可煩」，非五危之謂乎？其曰「不量眾寡，本乏刑德，失於訓練，
translation_en:
…bestowing the battle-axe of command so as to employ commanders effectively depends on the ruler’s ability to judge men. For generals command the troops, while the ruler commands the generals. If unsuitable men are appointed as generals, they lack the skill to deploy their forces and certainly cannot command the troops. If the ruler does not understand his generals, he lacks the means to control them; how, then, can he employ them? Allow me to set this out point by point.
Since antiquity, even in times of flourishing peace, states have never forgotten to anticipate trouble and take precautions. Thus they must select generals in tranquil times and employ them when trouble arises. Yet the means of selecting them are not narrowly confined to a single course: one need only examine whether their abilities are serviceable and employ them accordingly. Guan Zhong was promoted despite having shot at his ruler’s belt buckle, and Meng Ming despite suffering defeat: these men were not discarded because of their offenses. Rangju was raised from humble obscurity, and Wu Qi from the position of a sojourner: these men were not overlooked because they stood far from the centers of power. Su Qin formed the Vertical Alliance, and Zhang Yi the Horizontal Alliance: were they ever kept at a distance because of their deceit? Wei Qing rose from servitude, and Qubing from being an adopted son [?]: were they ever rejected because of their lowly status? In all these cases, their strengths were employed and their shortcomings set aside.
In selecting generals, the five qualities constitute the foundation: wisdom, trustworthiness, benevolence, courage, and strictness. The five forms of circumspection govern their practical application: orderly management, preparedness, decisiveness, vigilance, and restraint. title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
非理興怒法令不行不擇驍果非六敗之
謂乎又有九術者曰仁將義將禮將智將
信將步將騎將猛將大將則各有其術焉
又有十過者曰可暴可久可貴可勞可窘
可誑可侮可襲可事可欺是皆將之過焉
又有所謂十五貌不與衆情相應者有賢
而不肖者有温良而為盜者有貌恭敬而
心慢者有外廉謹而內無恭敬者有精而
無情者有湛湛而無誠者有好謀而無决
===
者有如果敢而不能者有悾悾而不信者
有恍惚而反忠實者有詭激而有功效者
有外勇而內怯者有肅肅而反易人者有
嚆嚆而反靜慤者有勢虚形劣而出外無
所不至無使不遂者凡是數者乃幾之藏
於心而貌之見於外最難知也為君上者
可不察之以八徵之法乎必問之以言以
觀其詞窮之以詞以觀其變與之間諜以
觀其誠明白顯問以觀其德使之以財以
punctuated: 非理興怒，法令不行，不擇驍果，非六敗之謂乎？又有九術者，曰仁將、義將、禮將、智將、信將、步將、騎將、猛將、大將，則各有其術焉。又有十過者，曰可暴、可久、可貴、可勞、可窘、可誑、可侮、可襲、可事、可欺，是皆將之過焉。又有所謂十五貌不與衆情相應者：有賢而不肖者，有温良而為盜者，有貌恭敬而心慢者，有外廉謹而內無恭敬者，有精而無情者，有湛湛而無誠者，有好謀而無决者，有如果敢而不能者，有悾悾而不信者，有恍惚而反忠實者，有詭激而有功效者，有外勇而內怯者，有肅肅而反易人者，有嚆嚆而反靜慤者，有勢虚形劣而出外無所不至、無使不遂者。凡是數者，乃幾之藏於心而貌之見於外，最難知也。為君上者，可不察之以八徵之法乎？必問之以言，以觀其詞；窮之以詞，以觀其變；與之間諜，以觀其誠；明白顯問，以觀其德；使之以財，以
translation_en:
… becoming angry without reason, failing to enforce laws and commands, and failing to select brave and resolute men—are these not what are called the six causes of defeat? There are also nine arts: those of the benevolent general, the righteous general, the ritually observant general, the wise general, the trustworthy general, the infantry general, the cavalry general, the fierce general, and the great general. Each has his own art. There are also ten faults: being susceptible to provocation, to being drawn into protracted operations, to enticement with honors, to exhaustion, to being placed in straits, to being misled, to humiliation, to surprise attack, to manipulation through service [?], and to deception. These are all faults of a general.
There are also the so-called fifteen appearances that do not correspond to people's actual dispositions. Some appear worthy but are unworthy; some appear gentle and good but are thieves; some appear respectful but are inwardly arrogant; some are outwardly scrupulous and circumspect but inwardly lack respect; some appear astute but lack genuine feeling; some appear profound but lack sincerity; some delight in planning but lack decisiveness; some seem bold and resolute [?] but lack ability; some appear sincere but are untrustworthy; some appear confused but are actually loyal and honest; some are eccentric and vehement yet achieve results; some are outwardly brave but inwardly cowardly; some appear solemn yet treat others lightly; some are loud and clamorous yet are actually calm and sincere; and some appear weak in bearing and inferior in physique, yet when sent out, reach every destination and accomplish every mission.

title: 成化十六年浙江鄉試錄
text:
觀其廉試之以色以觀其貞告之以難以
觀其勇醉之以酒以觀其態由是外與内
雖不同也而察之無所遁其情心與貌雖
不一也而察之無所售其詐將見英雄悉
歸於駕馭豪傑皆入於網羅勇者效其力
智者效其謀隨所任使而皆著夫敵愾禦
侮之功矣觀夫古之帝王負知人之明得
用將之道若周宣王能用吉甫以伐玁狁
而成中興之業漢高帝能用韓信以滅強
===
楚而建興劉之功唐太宗善用李勣而邊
陲以靖宋太祖善用曹彬而江南以平他
如方叔鄧禹之流郭子儀岳飛之輩莫不
有豐功偉蹟照耀簡冊而享祀於無窮也
豈不宜哉愚也爼豆儒生軍旅未究姑述
所聞以對不識執事以為何如
第四問
俞穩
同考試官訓導唐批歷叙江浙人物之盛鑿鑿皆
punctuated:
觀其廉，試之以色以觀其貞，告之以難以觀其勇，醉之以酒以觀其態。由是，外與内雖不同也，而察之無所遁其情；心與貌雖不一也，而察之無所售其詐。將見英雄悉歸於駕馭，豪傑皆入於網羅，勇者效其力，智者效其謀，隨所任使，而皆著夫敵愾禦侮之功矣。觀夫古之帝王，負知人之明，得用將之道，若周宣王能用吉甫以伐玁狁，而成中興之業；漢高帝能用韓信以滅強楚，而建興劉之功；唐太宗善用李勣，而邊陲以靖；宋太祖善用曹彬，而江南以平。他如方叔、鄧禹之流，郭子儀、岳飛之輩，莫不有豐功偉蹟，照耀簡冊，而享祀於無窮也，豈不宜哉？愚也，爼豆儒生，軍旅未究，姑述所聞以對，不識執事以為何如？

第四問
俞穩

同考試官訓導唐批：歷叙江浙人物之盛，鑿鑿皆
translation_en:
…to observe his integrity; test him with sensual allure to observe his steadfastness; tell him of difficulties to observe his courage; and make him drunk with wine to observe his bearing. In this way, although his outward conduct and inner character may differ, scrutiny leaves his true disposition nowhere to hide; although his mind and appearance may not agree, scrutiny leaves him no opportunity to practice deception. Then all heroes will come under your command, and all outstanding men will be gathered within your net. The courageous will contribute their strength, and the wise their strategies; whatever duties they are assigned, all will distinguish themselves in opposing the enemy and resisting aggression.

Consider the emperors and kings of antiquity who possessed the discernment to judge men and understood how to employ generals. King Xuan of Zhou employed Jifu to campaign against the Xianyun and thereby accomplished the restoration of his dynasty. Emperor Gao of Han employed Han Xin to destroy mighty Chu and thereby established the ascendancy of the Liu house. Emperor Taizong of Tang skillfully employed Li Ji, and the frontiers were pacified. Emperor Taizu of Song skillfully employed Cao Bin, and Jiangnan was subdued. Others, such as Fang Shu and Deng Yu, Guo Ziyi and Yue Fei, all achieved great deeds that shine in the historical records, and they receive sacrificial offerings for all time. Is this not fitting? I am but an ignorant Confucian scholar versed in sacrificial vessels and rites, and have not thoroughly studied military affairs. For now, I have related what I have heard in reply; I do not know what you, honored examiners, will think of it.
